diff --git a/pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py b/pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py
index 866db4e9a5..037774ba04 100644
--- a/pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py
+++ b/pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py
@@ -1098,6 +1098,9 @@ def _get_first_two_args_or_any(self, obj: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
     def _generate_schema_inner(self, obj: Any, origin: Any | None = PydanticUndefined) -> core_schema.CoreSchema:
         if typing_objects.is_self(obj):
             obj = self._resolve_self_type(obj)
+            # The resolved type can be a parametrized generic (e.g. `GenericDataclass[int]`),
+            # so the origin provided by the caller (computed on `Self`) is stale:
+            origin = get_origin(obj)
 
         origin = origin if origin is not PydanticUndefined else get_origin(obj)
 
diff --git a/tests/test_types_self.py b/tests/test_types_self.py
index d15367ed85..a8e6e6520f 100644
--- a/tests/test_types_self.py
+++ b/tests/test_types_self.py
@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@
 import re
 import sys
 import typing
+from typing import Generic, TypeVar
 
 import pytest
 import typing_extensions
@@ -9,6 +10,8 @@
 
 from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, PydanticUserError, TypeAdapter, ValidationError, computed_field, validate_call
 
+from .utils import dataclass_decorators
+
 self_types: list[TypeForm] = []
 ids: list[str] = []
 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
@@ -173,6 +176,44 @@ class Model(BaseModel):
         m.item.ref.x = 3
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('dataclass_decorator', **dataclass_decorators())
+def test_self_type_in_parametrized_generic_dataclass(Self, dataclass_decorator):
+    T = TypeVar('T')
+
+    @dataclass_decorator
+    class SelfRef(Generic[T]):
+        x: T
+        ref: Self | None = None
+
+    ta = TypeAdapter(SelfRef[int])
+    item = ta.validate_python({'x': '1', 'ref': {'x': '2'}})
+    assert item.x == 1
+    assert item.ref.x == 2
+    assert item.ref.ref is None
+
+
+def test_self_type_in_parametrized_generic_typed_dict(Self):
+    T = TypeVar('T')
+
+    class SelfRefTypedDict(TypedDict, Generic[T]):
+        x: T
+        ref: Self | None
+
+    ta = TypeAdapter(SelfRefTypedDict[int])
+    assert ta.validate_python({'x': '1', 'ref': {'x': '2', 'ref': None}}) == {'x': 1, 'ref': {'x': 2, 'ref': None}}
+
+
+def test_self_type_in_parametrized_generic_named_tuple(Self):
+    T = TypeVar('T')
+
+    class SelfRefNamedTuple(NamedTuple, Generic[T]):
+        x: T
+        ref: Self | None = None
+
+    ta = TypeAdapter(SelfRefNamedTuple[int])
+    assert ta.validate_python(('1', ('2',))) == (1, (2, None))
+
+
 def test_invalid_validate_call(Self):
     with pytest.raises(PydanticUserError, match='`typing.Self` is invalid in this context'):

guidelines:
[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

### Prerequisites

You'll need the following prerequisites:

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

### Installation and setup

Fork the repository on GitHu

[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

### Prerequisites

You'll need the following prerequisites:

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

@@ -1086,30 +1086,33 @@ def _get_first_two_args_or_any(self, obj: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
             return Any
         return args[0]
 
     def _get_first_two_args_or_any(self, obj: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
         args = self._get_args_resolving_forward_refs(obj)
         if not args:
             return (Any, Any)
         if len(args) < 2:
             origin = get_origin(obj)
             raise TypeError(f'Expected two type arguments for {origin}, got 1')
         return args[0], args[1]
 
     def _generate_schema_inner(self, obj: Any, origin: Any | None = PydanticUndefined) -> core_schema.CoreSchema:
         if typing_objects.is_self(obj):
             obj = self._resolve_self_type(obj)
+            # The resolved type can be a parametrized generic (e.g. `GenericDataclass[int]`),
+            # so the origin provided by the caller (computed on `Self`) is stale:
+            origin = get_origin(obj)
 
         origin = origin if origin is not PydanticUndefined else get_origin(obj)
 
         if is_union_origin(origin):
             return self._union_schema(obj)
 
         if typing_objects.is_annotated(origin):
             return self._annotated_schema(obj)
 
         if typing_objects.is_literal(origin):
             return self._literal_schema(obj)
 
         if isinstance(obj, dict):
             # we assume this is already a valid schema
             return obj  # type: ignore[return-value]

[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

### Prerequisites

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

### Prerequisites

You'll need the following prerequisites:

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

### Installation and setup

[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

### Prerequisites

You'll need the following prerequisites:

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

### Installation and setup

Fork the repository on GitHu

[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

### Prerequisites

You'll need the following prerequisites:

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

### Installation and setup

[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

You'll need the following prerequisites:

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

### Prerequisites

You'll need the following prerequisites:

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

### Installation and setup

Fork the repository on GitHu

diff --git a/pydantic/_internal/_docs_extraction.py b/pydantic/_internal/_docs_extraction.py
index 8808c1f08d..99dc246aca 100644
--- a/pydantic/_internal/_docs_extraction.py
+++ b/pydantic/_internal/_docs_extraction.py
@@ -25,30 +25,40 @@ def visit_Expr(self, node: ast.Expr) -> Any:
     def visit_AnnAssign(self, node: ast.AnnAssign) -> Any:
         if isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):
             self.target = node.target.id
 
     def visit_Expr(self, node: ast.Expr) -> Any:
         if (
             isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant)
             and isinstance(node.value.value, str)
             and self.previous_node_type is ast.AnnAssign
         ):
             docstring = inspect.cleandoc(node.value.value)
             if self.target:
                 self.attrs[self.target] = docstring
             self.target = None
 
+    # Don't look into nested classes and functions, as their attributes don't belong to the inspected class:
+    def visit_ClassDef(self, node: ast.ClassDef) -> Any:
+        pass
+
+    def visit_FunctionDef(self, node: ast.FunctionDef) -> Any:
+        pass
+
+    def visit_AsyncFunctionDef(self, node: ast.AsyncFunctionDef) -> Any:
+        pass
+
 
 def _dedent_source_lines(source: list[str]) -> str:
     # Required for nested class definitions, e.g. in a function block
     dedent_source = textwrap.dedent(''.join(source))
     if dedent_source.startswith((' ', '\t')):
         # We are in the case where there's a dedented (usually multiline) string
         # at a lower indentation level than the class itself. We wrap our class
         # in a function as a workaround.
         dedent_source = f'def dedent_workaround():\n{dedent_source}'
     return dedent_source
 
 
 def _extract_source_from_frame(cls: type[Any]) -> list[str] | None:
     frame = inspect.currentframe()
 
@@ -96,18 +106,23 @@ def extract_docstrings_from_cls(cls: type[Any], use_inspect: bool = False) -> di
         # On Python 3.13+, it will use the new `__firstlineno__` class attribute,
         # making it way more robust.
         try:
             source, _ = inspect.getsourcelines(cls)
         except (OSError, TypeError):  # pragma: no cover
             return {}
     else:
         # TODO remove this implementation when we drop support for Python 3.12:
         source = _extract_source_from_frame(cls)
 
     if not source:
         return {}
 
     dedent_source = _dedent_source_lines(source)
 
+    stmt = ast.parse(dedent_source).body[0]
+    if isinstance(stmt, ast.FunctionDef) and stmt.name == 'dedent_workaround':
+        # `_dedent_source_lines()` wrapped the class around the workaround function
+        stmt = stmt.body[0]
+
     visitor = DocstringVisitor()
-    visitor.visit(ast.parse(dedent_source))
+    visitor.generic_visit(stmt)
     return visitor.attrs
diff --git a/tests/test_docs_extraction.py b/tests/test_docs_extraction.py
index 8fa82ef85c..4cf7244004 100644
--- a/tests/test_docs_extraction.py
+++ b/tests/test_docs_extraction.py
@@ -197,6 +197,46 @@ class MyParameterizedModel(MyModel[int]):
     assert MyModel[int].model_fields['a'].description == 'A docs'
 
 
+def test_model_docs_nested_definitions():
+    """https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/14041"""
+
+    class Outer(BaseModel):
+        model_config = ConfigDict(use_attribute_docstrings=True)
+
+        a: int
+        """Outer A docs"""
+
+        b: int
+
+        c: int
+
+        class Inner(BaseModel):
+            model_config = ConfigDict(use_attribute_docstrings=True)
+
+            a: int
+            """Inner A docs"""
+
+            b: int
+            """Inner B docs"""
+
+            class Deeper(BaseModel):
+                model_config = ConfigDict(use_attribute_docstrings=True)
+
+                a: int
+                """Deeper A docs"""
+
+        def method(self) -> None:
+            c: int = 1  # noqa: F841
+            """Not a docstring for the `c` field"""
+
+    assert Outer.model_fields['a'].description == 'Outer A docs'
+    assert Outer.model_fields['b'].description is None
+    assert Outer.model_fields['c'].description is None
+    assert Outer.Inner.model_fields['a'].description == 'Inner A docs'
+    assert Outer.Inner.model_fields['b'].description == 'Inner B docs'
+    assert Outer.Inner.Deeper.model_fields['a'].description == 'Deeper A docs'
+
+
 def test_dataclass_no_docs_extraction():
     @pydantic_dataclass
     class MyModel:
guidelines:
[CONTRIBUTING.md]
We'd love you to contribute to Pydantic!

## Issues

Questions, feature requests and bug reports are all welcome as [discussions or issues](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/new/choose).
**However, to report a security vulnerability, please see our [security policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/policy).**

To make it as simple as possible for us to help you, please include the output of the following call in your issue:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.version; print(pydantic.version.version_info())"
```

If you're using Pydantic prior to **v2.0** please use:

```bash
python -c "import pydantic.utils; print(pydantic.utils.version_info())"
```

Please try to always include the above unless you're unable to install Pydantic or **know** it's not relevant
to your question or feature request.

## Pull Requests

It should be extremely simple to get started and create a Pull Request.

Unless your change is trivial (typo, docs tweak etc.), please create an issue to discuss the change before
creating a pull request. Any pull request fixing an existing issue without being assigned first will be
automatically closed.

!!! note "Pydantic V1 is in maintenance mode"
    Pydantic v1 is in maintenance mode, meaning that only bug fixes and security fixes will be accepted.
    New features should be targeted at Pydantic v2.

    To submit a fix to Pydantic v1, use the [`1.10.X-fixes`](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/1.10.X-fixes) as a target branch.

To make contributing as easy and fast as possible, you'll want to run tests and linting locally. Luckily,
Pydantic has few dependencies, doesn't require compiling and tests don't need access to databases, etc.
Because of this, setting up and running the tests should be very simple.

!!! tip
    **tl;dr**: use `make format` to fix formatting, `make` to run tests and linting and `make docs`
    to build the docs.

## AI policy

We welcome the use of AI when contributing to Pydantic. However, users should certify that they fully understand the code being submitted.
We reserve the right to close any pull request at our discretion, without further justification. This includes, but is not limited to, cases where:

* the contribution does not meet our quality standards,
* the author appears to be mass-submitting pull requests across multiple repositories (spam),
* the pull request description is AI generated *and* incoherent or nonsensical.

Such behavior can also result in a permanent ban from the organization.

### Prerequisites

You'll need the following prerequisites:

* Any Python version between **Python 3.10 and 3.14**
* [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
* [**git**](https://git-scm.com/) - For version control
* [**make**](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) - For running development commands (or use `nmake` on Windows)
* [**Rust**](https://rustup.rs/) - Rust stable (or nightly for coverage)

### Installation and setup

Fork the repository on GitHu

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import collections.abc
import typing
from typing import Any

from pydantic_core import PydanticOmit, core_schema

from ._typing_extra import is_namedtuple

SEQUENCE_ORIGIN_MAP: dict[Any, Any] = {
    typing.Deque: collections.deque,  # noqa: UP006
    collections.deque: collections.deque,
    list: list,
    typing.List: list,  # noqa: UP006
    tuple: tuple,
    typing.Tuple: tuple,  # noqa: UP006
    set: set,
    typing.AbstractSet: set,
    typing.Set: set,  # noqa: UP006
    frozenset: frozenset,
    typing.FrozenSet: frozenset,  # noqa: UP006
    typing.Sequence: list,
    typing.MutableSequence: list,
    typing.MutableSet: set,
    # this doesn't handle subclasses of these
    # parametrized typing.Set creates one of these
    collections.abc.MutableSet: set,
    collections.abc.Set: frozenset,
}


def serialize_sequence_via_list(
    v: Any, handler: core_schema.SerializerFunctionWrapHandler, info: core_schema.SerializationInfo
) -> Any:
    items: list[Any] = []

    value_type = type(v)
    mapped_origin = SEQUENCE_ORIGIN_MAP.get(value_type)
    if mapped_origin is None and not is_namedtuple(value_type):
        # we shouldn't hit this branch, should probably add a serialization error or something
        return v

    for index, item in enumerate(v):
        try:
            item_v = handler(item, index)
        except PydanticOmit:  # noqa: PERF203
            pass
        else:
            items.append(item_v)

    if info.mode_is_json():
        return items
    elif mapped_origin is not None:
        return mapped_origin(items)
    else:
        # named tuple: if some items were excluded, it can't be re-created
        return value_type(*items) if len(items) == len(v) else tuple(items)

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import collections.abc
import typing
from typing import Any

from pydantic_core import PydanticOmit, core_schema

from ._typing_extra import is_namedtuple

SEQUENCE_ORIGIN_MAP: dict[Any, Any] = {
    typing.Deque: collections.deque,  # noqa: UP006
    collections.deque: collections.deque,
    list: list,
    typing.List: list,  # noqa: UP006
    tuple: tuple,
    typing.Tuple: tuple,  # noqa: UP006
    set: set,
    typing.AbstractSet: set,
    typing.Set: set,  # noqa: UP006
    frozenset: frozenset,
    typing.FrozenSet: frozenset,  # noqa: UP006
    typing.Sequence: list,
    typing.MutableSequence: list,
    typing.MutableSet: set,
    # this doesn't handle subclasses of these
    # parametrized typing.Set creates one of these
    collections.abc.MutableSet: set,
    collections.abc.Set: frozenset,
}


def serialize_sequence_via_list(
    v: Any, handler: core_schema.SerializerFunctionWrapHandler, info: core_schema.SerializationInfo
) -> Any:
    items: list[Any] = []

    value_type = type(v)
    mapped_origin = SEQUENCE_ORIGIN_MAP.get(value_type)
    if mapped_origin is None and not is_namedtuple(value_type):
        # we shouldn't hit this branch, should probably add a serialization error or something
        return v

    for index, item in enumerate(v):
        try:
            item_v = handler(item, index)
        except PydanticOmit:  # noqa: PERF203
            pass
        else:
            items.append(item_v)

    if info.mode_is_json():
        return items
    elif mapped_origin is not None:
        return mapped_origin(items)
    else:
        # named tuple: if some items were excluded, it can't be re-created
        return value_type(*items) if len(items) == len(v) else tuple(items)

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import collections.abc
import typing
from typing import Any

from pydantic_core import PydanticOmit, core_schema

from ._typing_extra import is_namedtuple

SEQUENCE_ORIGIN_MAP: dict[Any, Any] = {
    typing.Deque: collections.deque,  # noqa: UP006
    collections.deque: collections.deque,
    list: list,
    typing.List: list,  # noqa: UP006
    tuple: tuple,
    typing.Tuple: tuple,  # noqa: UP006
    set: set,
    typing.AbstractSet: set,
    typing.Set: set,  # noqa: UP006
    frozenset: frozenset,
    typing.FrozenSet: frozenset,  # noqa: UP006
    typing.Sequence: list,
    typing.MutableSequence: list,
    typing.MutableSet: set,
    # this doesn't handle subclasses of these
    # parametrized typing.Set creates one of these
    collections.abc.MutableSet: set,
    collections.abc.Set: frozenset,
}


def serialize_sequence_via_list(
    v: Any, handler: core_schema.SerializerFunctionWrapHandler, info: core_schema.SerializationInfo
) -> Any:
    items: list[Any] = []

    value_type = type(v)
    mapped_origin = SEQUENCE_ORIGIN_MAP.get(value_type)
    if mapped_origin is None and not is_namedtuple(value_type):
        # we shouldn't hit this branch, should probably add a serialization error or something
        return v

    for index, item in enumerate(v):
        try:
            item_v = handler(item, index)
        except PydanticOmit:  # noqa: PERF203
            pass
        else:
            items.append(item_v)

    if info.mode_is_json():
        return items
    elif mapped_origin is not None:
        return mapped_origin(items)
    else:
        # named tuple: if some items were excluded, it can't be re-created
        return value_type(*items) if len(items) == len(v) else tuple(items)

Fix unpickling of generic classes defined in separate module

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13991.

Note that the following no longer resolves:

```python
# models.py
from typing import Generic, TypeVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

T = TypeVar('T')


class Response(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    result: T
    f: 'F'


import app  # e.g. circular import

F = str


# app.py
from models import Response

IntResponse = Response[int]  # parametrized while models.py is still being loaded


# main.py
import app

app.IntResponse(result=1, f='f')
```

As it only coincidentally worked because we were using the wrong `__module__`, and so the "wrong" module would be used in `rebuild_model_fields()`. This wasn't working for "normal" classes either:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/22c4317a5d51d71344275259b4e536c4a90fe53b/tests/test_forward_ref.py#L1147-L1174

Note that the circular import is required to make it fail (which is a very unusual scenario, and why I accept the regression), as otherwise the generic parameterization calls `origin.model_rebuild()` successfully.

On the other hand, it now supports another (potentially more common) use case, see `test_resolve_forward_ref_type_argument_in_parametrizing_module()`.

Fix unpickling of generic classes defined in separate module

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13991.

Note that the following no longer resolves:

```python
# models.py
from typing import Generic, TypeVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

T = TypeVar('T')


class Response(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    result: T
    f: 'F'


import app  # e.g. circular import

F = str


# app.py
from models import Response

IntResponse = Response[int]  # parametrized while models.py is still being loaded


# main.py
import app

app.IntResponse(result=1, f='f')
```

As it only coincidentally worked because we were using the wrong `__module__`, and so the "wrong" module would be used in `rebuild_model_fields()`. This wasn't working for "normal" classes either:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/22c4317a5d51d71344275259b4e536c4a90fe53b/tests/test_forward_ref.py#L1147-L1174

Note that the circular import is required to make it fail (which is a very unusual scenario, and why I accept the regression), as otherwise the generic parameterization calls `origin.model_rebuild()` successfully.

On the other hand, it now supports another (potentially more common) use case, see `test_resolve_forward_ref_type_argument_in_parametrizing_module()`.

Fix unpickling of generic classes defined in separate module

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13991.

Note that the following no longer resolves:

```python
# models.py
from typing import Generic, TypeVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

T = TypeVar('T')


class Response(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    result: T
    f: 'F'


import app  # e.g. circular import

F = str


# app.py
from models import Response

IntResponse = Response[int]  # parametrized while models.py is still being loaded


# main.py
import app

app.IntResponse(result=1, f='f')
```

As it only coincidentally worked because we were using the wrong `__module__`, and so the "wrong" module would be used in `rebuild_model_fields()`. This wasn't working for "normal" classes either:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/22c4317a5d51d71344275259b4e536c4a90fe53b/tests/test_forward_ref.py#L1147-L1174

Note that the circular import is required to make it fail (which is a very unusual scenario, and why I accept the regression), as otherwise the generic parameterization calls `origin.model_rebuild()` successfully.

On the other hand, it now supports another (potentially more common) use case, see `test_resolve_forward_ref_type_argument_in_parametrizing_module()`.

Fix unpickling of generic classes defined in separate module

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13991.

Note that the following no longer resolves:

```python
# models.py
from typing import Generic, TypeVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

T = TypeVar('T')


class Response(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    result: T
    f: 'F'


import app  # e.g. circular import

F = str


# app.py
from models import Response

IntResponse = Response[int]  # parametrized while models.py is still being loaded


# main.py
import app

app.IntResponse(result=1, f='f')
```

As it only coincidentally worked because we were using the wrong `__module__`, and so the "wrong" module would be used in `rebuild_model_fields()`. This wasn't working for "normal" classes either:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/22c4317a5d51d71344275259b4e536c4a90fe53b/tests/test_forward_ref.py#L1147-L1174

Note that the circular import is required to make it fail (which is a very unusual scenario, and why I accept the regression), as otherwise the generic parameterization calls `origin.model_rebuild()` successfully.

On the other hand, it now supports another (potentially more common) use case, see `test_resolve_forward_ref_type_argument_in_parametrizing_module()`.

        super().__setitem__(key, value)

            to_remove = list(self.keys())[:excess]

        Taken from https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.html#collections.ChainMap,
        with some light modifications for this use case.

        def clear(self) -> None:

Fix unpickling of generic classes defined in separate module

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13991.

Note that the following no longer resolves:

```python
# models.py
from typing import Generic, TypeVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

T = TypeVar('T')


class Response(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    result: T
    f: 'F'


import app  # e.g. circular import

F = str


# app.py
from models import Response

IntResponse = Response[int]  # parametrized while models.py is still being loaded


# main.py
import app

app.IntResponse(result=1, f='f')
```

As it only coincidentally worked because we were using the wrong `__module__`, and so the "wrong" module would be used in `rebuild_model_fields()`. This wasn't working for "normal" classes either:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/22c4317a5d51d71344275259b4e536c4a90fe53b/tests/test_forward_ref.py#L1147-L1174

Note that the circular import is required to make it fail (which is a very unusual scenario, and why I accept the regression), as otherwise the generic parameterization calls `origin.model_rebuild()` successfully.

On the other hand, it now supports another (potentially more common) use case, see `test_resolve_forward_ref_type_argument_in_parametrizing_module()`.

Fix unpickling of generic classes defined in separate module

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13991.

Note that the following no longer resolves:

```python
# models.py
from typing import Generic, TypeVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

T = TypeVar('T')


class Response(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    result: T
    f: 'F'


import app  # e.g. circular import

F = str


# app.py
from models import Response

IntResponse = Response[int]  # parametrized while models.py is still being loaded


# main.py
import app

app.IntResponse(result=1, f='f')
```

As it only coincidentally worked because we were using the wrong `__module__`, and so the "wrong" module would be used in `rebuild_model_fields()`. This wasn't working for "normal" classes either:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/22c4317a5d51d71344275259b4e536c4a90fe53b/tests/test_forward_ref.py#L1147-L1174

Note that the circular import is required to make it fail (which is a very unusual scenario, and why I accept the regression), as otherwise the generic parameterization calls `origin.model_rebuild()` successfully.

On the other hand, it now supports another (potentially more common) use case, see `test_resolve_forward_ref_type_argument_in_parametrizing_module()`.

 ## About "Form Fields" { #about-form-fields }
 
 The way HTML forms (`<form></form>`) send the data to the server normally uses a "special" encoding for that data, it's different from JSON.
 
 **FastAPI** will make sure to read that data from the right place instead of JSON.
 
 /// note | Technical Details
 
 Data from forms is normally encoded using the "media type" `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
 
 But when the form includes files, it is encoded as `multipart/form-data`. You'll read about handling files in the next chapter.
 
+You can use `Form(media_type="multipart/form-data")` to describe a multipart form in OpenAPI. Setting it on one parameter is enough when combining form parameters or models.
+

 ///

 Use `Form` to declare form data input parameters.

+from io import BytesIO
+from typing import Annotated
+
+import pytest
+from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, File, UploadFile
+from fastapi.dependencies.utils import _read_file_bytes
+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "content",
+    [
+        pytest.param(b"hello", id="memory"),
+        pytest.param(b"x" * (1024 * 1024 + 1), id="disk"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_file_bytes_shared_by_dependency_and_endpoint(content: bytes):
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    def inspect_file(file: Annotated[bytes, File()]):
+        return file.decode()
+
+    @app.post("/")
+    def upload(
+        inspected: Annotated[str, Depends(inspect_file)],
+        file: Annotated[bytes, File()],
+    ):
+        return {"dependency": inspected, "endpoint": file.decode()}
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.post("/", files={"file": ("hello.txt", content)})
+    assert response.json() == {
+        "dependency": content.decode(),
+        "endpoint": content.decode(),
+    }
+
+
+def test_file_bytes_list_shared_by_dependency_and_endpoint():
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    def inspect_files(files: Annotated[list[bytes], File()]):
+        return [file.decode() for file in files]
+
+    @app.post("/")
+    def upload(
+        inspected: Annotated[list[str], Depends(inspect_files)],
+        files: Annotated[list[bytes], File()],
+    ):
+        return {"dependency": inspected, "endpoint": [file.decode() for file in files]}
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.post(
+        "/",
+        files=[
+            ("files", ("one.txt", b"one")),
+            ("files", ("two.txt", b"two")),
+        ],
+    )
+    assert response.json() == {
+        "dependency": ["one", "two"],
+        "endpoint": ["one", "two"],
+    }
+
+
+def test_bytes_dependency_preserves_upload_file_for_endpoint():
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    def inspect_file(file: Annotated[bytes, File()]):
+        return file.decode()
+
+    @app.post("/")
+    async def upload(
+        inspected: Annotated[str, Depends(inspect_file)],
+        file: Annotated[UploadFile, File()],
+    ):
+        content = await file.read()
+        second_read = await file.read()
+        return {
+            "dependency": inspected,
+            "endpoint": content.decode(),
+            "second_read": second_read.decode(),
+        }
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.post("/", files={"file": ("hello.txt", b"hello")})
+    assert response.json() == {
+        "dependency": "hello",
+        "endpoint": "hello",
+        "second_read": "",
+    }
+
+
+def test_automatic_file_read_preserves_nonzero_position():
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    async def read_prefix(file: Annotated[UploadFile, File()]):
+        return (await file.read(2)).decode()
+
+    def inspect_remainder(
+        prefix: Annotated[str, Depends(read_prefix)],
+        file: Annotated[bytes, File()],
+    ):
+        return {"prefix": prefix, "remainder": file.decode()}
+
+    @app.post("/")
+    async def upload(
+        inspected: Annotated[dict[str, str], Depends(inspect_remainder)],
+        file: Annotated[UploadFile, File()],
+    ):
+        position = file.file.tell()
+        remainder = await file.read()
+        return {
+            "dependency": inspected,
+            "position": position,
+            "remainder": remainder.decode(),
+        }
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.post("/", files={"file": ("hello.txt", b"hello")})
+    assert response.json() == {
+        "dependency": {"prefix": "he", "remainder": "llo"},
+        "position": 2,
+        "remainder": "llo",
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.anyio

+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,

+    with BytesIO(b"hello") as stream:
+        file = UploadFile(file=stream)
+        stream.seek(2)
+
+        async def failing_read(size: int = -1) -> bytes:
+            stream.read(1)
+            raise OSError("read failed")
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(file, "read", failing_read)
+        with pytest.raises(OSError, match="read failed"):
+            await _read_file_bytes(file)
+

+from io import BytesIO

+
+

+)

+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    def inspect_file(file: Annotated[bytes, File()]):

+

+        file: Annotated[bytes, File()],

+        return {"dependency": inspected, "endpoint": file.decode()}
+
+    client = TestClient(app)

+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json() == {
+        "dependency": content.decode(),
+        "endpoint": content.decode(),
+    }
+
+

+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    def inspect_files(files: Annotated[list[bytes], File()]):
+        return [file.decode() for file in files]
+
+    @app.post("/")
+    def upload(
+        inspected: Annotated[list[str], Depends(inspect_files)],
+        files: Annotated[list[bytes], File()],
+    ):
+        return {"dependency": inspected, "endpoint": [file.decode() for file in files]}
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.post(

+            ("files", ("one.txt", b"one")),
+            ("files", ("two.txt", b"two")),
+        ],
+    )

+    assert response.json() == {
+        "dependency": ["one", "two"],
+        "endpoint": ["one", "two"],
+    }
+
+
+def test_bytes_dependency_preserves_upload_file_for_endpoint():
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    def inspect_file(file: Annotated[bytes, File()]):
+        return file.decode()
+
+    @app.post("/")
+    async def upload(
+        inspected: Annotated[str, Depends(inspect_file)],
+        file: Annotated[UploadFile, File()],

+        second_read = await file.read()
+        return {
+            "dependency": inspected,
+            "endpoint": content.decode(),
+            "second_read": second_read.decode(),
+        }
+

    try:
        from python_multipart import __version__

        # Import an attribute that can be mocked/deleted in testing
        assert __version__ > "0.0.12"
    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:

            from multipart import (  # type: ignore[no-redef,import-untyped]

                assert parse_options_header
            except ImportError:
                logger.error(multipart_incorrect_install_error)
                raise RuntimeError(multipart_incorrect_install_error) from None

        assert __version__ > "0.0.12"
    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:

    try:
        from python_multipart import __version__

        # Import an attribute that can be mocked/deleted in testing
        assert __version__ > "0.0.12"
    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:
            # __version__ is available in both multiparts, and can be mocked
            from multipart import (  # type: ignore[no-redef,import-untyped]
                __version__,

                from multipart.multipart import (  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

                assert parse_options_header
            except ImportError:
                logger.error(multipart_incorrect_install_error)
                raise RuntimeError(multipart_incorrect_install_error) from None

    try:

        assert __version__ > "0.0.12"
    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:

def ensure_multipart_is_installed() -> None:
    try:
        from python_multipart import __version__

        # Import an attribute that can be mocked/deleted in testing
        assert __version__ > "0.0.12"
    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:
            # __version__ is available in both multiparts, and can be mocked
            from multipart import (  # type: ignore[no-redef,import-untyped]
                __version__,
            )

            assert __version__
            try:
                # parse_options_header is only available in the right multipart
                from multipart.multipart import (  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
                    parse_options_header,
                )

                assert parse_options_header
            except ImportError:
                logger.error(multipart_incorrect_install_error)
                raise RuntimeError(multipart_incorrect_install_error) from None
        except ImportError:
            logger.error(multipart_not_installed_error)
            raise RuntimeError(multipart_not_installed_error) from None

    try:

        assert __version__ > "0.0.12"
    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:
            # __version__ is available in both multiparts, and can be mocked
            from multipart import (  # type: ignore[no-redef,import-untyped]

    'You can install "python-multipart" with: \n\n'

)

def ensure_multipart_is_installed() -> None:
    try:
        from python_multipart import __version__

        # Import an attribute that can be mocked/deleted in testing
        assert __version__ > "0.0.12"
    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:
            # __version__ is available in both multiparts, and can be mocked
            from multipart import (  # type: ignore[no-redef,import-untyped]
                __version__,
            )

            assert __version__
            try:
                # parse_options_header is only available in the right multipart
                from multipart.multipart import (  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
                    parse_options_header,
                )

                assert parse_options_header
            except ImportError:
                logger.error(multipart_incorrect_install_error)
                raise RuntimeError(multipart_incorrect_install_error) from None
        except ImportError:
            logger.error(multipart_not_installed_error)
            raise RuntimeError(multipart_not_installed_error) from None

+app = FastAPI()
+router = APIRouter()
+identifier_path = Path(
+    alias="unused",
+    validation_alias=AliasChoices("item_id", "id"),
+    ge=1,
+)
+Identifier = Annotated[int, identifier_path]
+
+
+def get_identifier(value: Identifier):
+    return value
+
+
+@router.get("/")
+def read_item(value: Annotated[int, Depends(get_identifier)]):
+    return value
+
+
+app.include_router(router, prefix="/items/{item_id}")
+app.include_router(router, prefix="/legacy-items/{id}")
+
+
+@app.websocket("/ws/{id}")
+async def read_websocket(
+    websocket: WebSocket, value: Annotated[int, Depends(get_identifier)]
+):
+    await websocket.accept()
+    await websocket.send_json(value)
+    await websocket.close()
+
+
+client = TestClient(app)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", ["/items", "/legacy-items"])
+def test_dependency_alias_choices_follow_router_prefix(prefix: str):
+    response = client.get(f"{prefix}/1/")
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json() == 1
+    assert identifier_path.validation_alias == AliasChoices("item_id", "id")
+    assert identifier_path.alias == "unused"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "prefix, alias", [("/items", "item_id"), ("/legacy-items", "id")]
+)
+def test_invalid_value_uses_route_parameter_name(prefix: str, alias: str):
+    response = client.get(f"{prefix}/invalid/")
+    assert response.status_code == 422
+    assert response.json() == {
+        "detail": [
+            {
+                "type": "int_parsing",
+                "loc": ["path", alias],
+                "msg": "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer",
+                "input": "invalid",
+            }
+        ]
+    }
+
+
+def test_selected_alias_preserves_constraints():
+    response = client.get("/legacy-items/0/")
+    assert response.status_code == 422
+    assert response.json() == {
+        "detail": [
+            {
+                "type": "greater_than_equal",
+                "loc": ["path", "id"],
+                "msg": "Input should be greater than or equal to 1",
+                "input": "0",
+                "ctx": {"ge": 1},
+            }
+        ]
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("alias", ["first", "second"])
+def test_individual_path_alias_choices(alias: str):
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    @app.get("/{" + alias + "}")
+    def read(
+        value: Annotated[int, Path(validation_alias=AliasChoices("first", "second"))],
+    ):
+        return value
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.get("/1")
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json() == 1
+
+
+def test_multiple_matching_choices_follow_declaration_order():
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    @app.get("/{second}/{first}")
+    def read(
+        value: Annotated[
+            int, Path(alias="second", validation_alias=AliasChoices("first", "second"))
+        ],
+        second: str,
+    ):
+        return {"value": value, "second": second}
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.get("/2/1")
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json() == {"value": 1, "second": "2"}
+    response = client.get("/2/invalid")
+    assert response.status_code == 422
+    assert response.json() == {
+        "detail": [
+            {
+                "type": "int_parsing",
+                "loc": ["path", "first"],
+                "msg": "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer",
+                "input": "invalid",
+            }
+        ]
+    }
+
+
+def test_unmatched_choices_preserve_explicit_alias():
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    @app.get("/{legacy}")
+    def read(
+        value: Annotated[
+            int, Path(alias="legacy", validation_alias=AliasChoices("first", "second"))
+        ],
+    ):
+        return value
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.get("/1")
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json() == 1
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "validation_alias",
+    [AliasPath("value"), AliasChoices("first", AliasPath("value"))],
+)
+def test_alias_path_extraction_is_unchanged(validation_alias):
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    @app.get("/{first}/{value}")
+    def read(
+        value: Annotated[int, Path(validation_alias=validation_alias)], first: int
+    ):
+        return {"value": value, "first": first}
+
+    client = TestClient(app)
+    response = client.get("/1/2")
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json() == {"value": 2, "first": 1}
+
+
+def test_websocket_dependency_uses_matching_alias():
+    with client.websocket_connect("/ws/1") as websocket:
+        assert websocket.receive_json() == 1
+

    try:

    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:

    try:

    except (ImportError, AssertionError):
        try:

task:
Fix node duration formatting when rounding crosses a unit boundary

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"RonnyPfannschmidt"} -->
_Requested by **Ronny** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvR?thread=cmsg_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvRGXe3toUv4HSfP5aWh397m2)_

🤖 Written by Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code for the pytest maintainers; I prompted it, it did the work, I read it.

**Merge strategy: squash.**

Before: with `console_output_style = times`, a duration just under a unit boundary was printed with too many digits, e.g. 0.99996ms as `1000.0us` and 59.9996s as `0m 60s`. `TestProgressOutputStyle::test_times` failed on main because of this ([windows-py311 job](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/actions/runs/37465844384/job/112277341632), output `test_foo.py .....  1000.0us`).

After: the same durations print as `1.000ms` and `1m 0s`.

How: `format_node_duration` now formats the value first and only keeps a unit if the rounded number stays below that unit's limit, otherwise it moves to the next one. Minutes and hours are computed from the rounded whole seconds. New parametrized cases cover each boundary; all of them fail on main.

No library was used: `humanize` and `humanfriendly` produce long-form text ("999 milliseconds and 960 microseconds"), not the compact at-most-7-character column this output needs, and `humanfriendly.format_timespan(59.9996)` has the same rounding issue ("60 seconds").

- [x] Tests added
- [x] AI agent credited in `Co-authored-by` trailer
- [x] Changelog entry

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"RonnyPfannschmidt"} -->
_Requested by **Ronny** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvR?thread=cmsg_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvRGXe3toUv4HSfP5aWh397m2)_

🤖 Written by Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code for the pytest maintainers; I prompted it, it did the work, I read it.

**Merge strategy: squash.**

Before: with `console_output_style = times`, a duration just under a unit boundary was printed with too many digits, e.g. 0.99996ms as `1000.0us` and 59.9996s as `0m 60s`. `TestProgressOutputStyle::test_times` failed on main because of this ([windows-py311 job](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/actions/runs/37465844384/job/112277341632), output `test_foo.py .....  1000.0us`).

After: the same durations print as `1.000ms` and `1m 0s`.

No library was used: `humanize` and `humanfriendly` produce long-form text ("999 milliseconds and 960 microseconds"), not the compact at-most-7-character column this output needs, and `humanfriendly.format_timespan(59.9996)` has the same rounding issue ("60 seconds").

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"RonnyPfannschmidt"} -->
_Requested by **Ronny** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvR?thread=cmsg_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvRGXe3toUv4HSfP5aWh397m2)_

🤖 Written by Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code for the pytest maintainers; I prompted it, it did the work, I read it.

**Merge strategy: squash.**

Before: with `console_output_style = times`, a duration just under a unit boundary was printed with too many digits, e.g. 0.99996ms as `1000.0us` and 59.9996s as `0m 60s`. `TestProgressOutputStyle::test_times` failed on main because of this ([windows-py311 job](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/actions/runs/37465844384/job/112277341632), output `test_foo.py .....  1000.0us`).

After: the same durations print as `1.000ms` and `1m 0s`.

How: `format_node_duration` now formats the value first and only keeps a unit if the rounded number stays below that unit's limit, otherwise it moves to the next one. Minutes and hours are computed from the rounded whole seconds. New parametrized cases cover each boundary; all of them fail on main.

No library was used: `humanize` and `humanfriendly` produce long-form text ("999 milliseconds and 960 microseconds"), not the compact at-most-7-character column this output needs, and `humanfriendly.format_timespan(59.9996)` has the same rounding issue ("60 seconds").

- [x] Tests added
- [x] AI agent credited in `Co-authored-by` trailer
- [x] Changelog entry

Assertion rewriting issue with editable-installed plugins

### Problem

When I look into/debug external plugins, my workflow is:

- Create a venv
- Run `pip install -e .` (this is with a recent pip and setuptools backend, so is using "new style" [PEP 660](https://peps.python.org/pep-0660/) editable installs. `editable_mode=strict` doesn't seem to make a difference)
- Run `pytest`

While doing this for several plugins recently (e.g. pytest-asyncio), I've noticed pytest issues a warning:

```
../../../../home/ran/src/pytest/src/_pytest/config/__init__.py:759
  /home/ran/src/pytest/src/_pytest/config/__init__.py:759: PytestAssertRewriteWarning: Module already imported so cannot be rewritten: pytest_asyncio
    self.import_plugin(import_spec)
```

### Analysis

This is my understanding of why this happens:

- pytest's assertion rewriting requires that a module be marked for rewrite before it is imported.
- For external plugins this is done by the [_mark_plugins_for_rewrite](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/13eacdad8ac434b4336cf1e6496869815a6457c7/src/_pytest/config/__init__.py#L1211) function.
- This function iterates over all files of all installed distributions which have a `pytest11` entry point, and marks their modules for rewrite if necessary.

This ends up now working with my workflow because the `distribution.files` doesn't contain any of the actual package python files. Relevant issues: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/96144 https://github.com/pypa/packaging-problems/issues/620

Currently there is no solution from the packaging side. It might be possible to add a workaround on the pytest side, I'm not sure.
description:
## Problem

`_mark_plugins_for_rewrite()` decides which modules to mark for assertion rewriting by walking the Python files recorded in each plugin distribution's metadata. A PEP 660 editable install doesn't record them — `dist.files` only holds the `__editable__*.pth` shim and the `dist-info` entries — so nothing matches and the plugin never gets marked.

The effect is that assertions inside a plugin stop being rewritten as soon as it is installed with `pip install -e .`, which is the usual way to work on one. With a plugin that asserts in its own helpers:

```python
# myplug/helper.py
def compare(got, want):
    assert got == want
```

```
# pip install .
E       AssertionError: assert {'a': 1, 'b': 2} == {'a': 1, 'b': 3}

# pip install -e .
E       AssertionError
```

## Fix

When a distribution is installed in editable mode and its recorded files yield no rewritable module, fall back to the top-level package of its `pytest11` entry points. Editable mode is read from `direct_url.json` (PEP 610), so regular installs keep taking the existing file-based path untouched.

The `direct_url.json` gate matters. Without it the fallback also fires for distributions that simply record no files, which a number of tests in the suite construct, and 13 of them change behaviour.

## Tests

The new test covers three distributions: an editable one, a regular install from a local directory, and one installed from an index with no `direct_url.json`. Only the editable case fails on `main`.

Fixes #11783

description:
## Problem

`_mark_plugins_for_rewrite()` decides which modules to mark for assertion rewriting by walking the Python files recorded in each plugin distribution's metadata. A PEP 660 editable install doesn't record them — `dist.files` only holds the `__editable__*.pth` shim and the `dist-info` entries — so nothing matches and the plugin never gets marked.

The effect is that assertions inside a plugin stop being rewritten as soon as it is installed with `pip install -e .`, which is the usual way to work on one. With a plugin that asserts in its own helpers:

```python
# myplug/helper.py
def compare(got, want):
    assert got == want
```

```
# pip install .
E       AssertionError: assert {'a': 1, 'b': 2} == {'a': 1, 'b': 3}

# pip install -e .
E       AssertionError
```

## Fix

When a distribution is installed in editable mode and its recorded files yield no rewritable module, fall back to the top-level package of its `pytest11` entry points. Editable mode is read from `direct_url.json` (PEP 610), so regular installs keep taking the existing file-based path untouched.

The `direct_url.json` gate matters. Without it the fallback also fires for distributions that simply record no files, which a number of tests in the suite construct, and 13 of them change behaviour.

## Tests

The new test covers three distributions: an editable one, a regular install from a local directory, and one installed from an index with no `direct_url.json`. Only the editable case fails on `main`.

Fixes #11783
