Bug: es, fr, he, hr and lt locales are missing the map entry in Sizable, so z.map() size errors lose their unit

## Summary

The `es`, `fr`, `he`, `hr` and `lt` locales have no `map` entry in their `Sizable` table. As a result, `z.map().min()/max()/size()` errors fall through to the generic comparison wording, without the unit, and in `lt` they end with `undefined`. The matching `set` messages in the same locales are correct.

## Reproduction

1. `npm i zod@4.6.6`
2. Run with `node repro.mjs`:

```js
import * as z from "zod";
for (const l of ["en", "es", "fr", "he", "hr", "lt"]) {
  z.config(z.locales[l]());
  const m = z.map(z.string(), z.number()).max(1).safeParse(new Map([["a", 1], ["b", 2]])).error.issues[0].message;
  const s = z.set(z.string()).max(1).safeParse(new Set(["a", "b"])).error.issues[0].message;
  console.log(`${l} map: ${m}  |  set: ${s}`);
}
```

3. The bug triggers on any `too_big` / `too_small` issue with `origin: "map"` under one of those five locales.

## Actual behavior

```
en map: Too big: expected map to have <=1 entries  |  set: Too big: expected set to have <=1 items
es map: Demasiado grande: se esperaba que mapa fuera <=1  |  set: Demasiado grande: se esperaba que conjunto tuviera <=1 elementos
fr map: Trop grand : map doit être <=1  |  set: Trop grand : ensemble doit avoir <=1 éléments
he map: גדול מדי: המפה (Map) צריכה להיות <=1  |  set: גדול מדי: הקבוצה (Set) צריכה להכיל 1 פריטים או פחות
hr map: Preveliko: očekivano da mapa bude <=1  |  set: Preveliko: očekivano da skup ima <=1 stavki
lt map: Map turi būti ne didesnis kaip 1 undefined  |  set: Set turi turėti ne daugiau kaip 1 elementą
```

## Expected behavior

Map size errors should state the unit (entries), the way `en` and the `set` messages in the same locales do, e.g. `se esperaba que mapa tuviera <=1 entradas`.

## Environment

- Version/commit: zod 4.6.6 (npm), also present on `main` at 284243fb
- OS: Ubuntu Linux, Node v24.21.0
- Relevant configuration: `z.config(z.locales.es())` (or `fr` / `he` / `hr` / `lt`)

## Evidence

I compared each locale's `Sizable` keys against `en.ts` (`string`, `file`, `array`, `set`, `map`). These five lack `map`, e.g. `packages/zod/src/v4/locales/es.ts:6-11`:

```ts
const Sizable: Record<string, { unit: string; verb: string }> = {
  string: { unit: "caracteres", verb: "tener" },
  file: { unit: "bytes", verb: "tener" },
  array: { unit: "elementos", verb: "tener" },
  set: { unit: "elementos", verb: "tener" },
};
```

## Additional context

- Confirmed: the five locales and their output above. Every other locale has a `map` entry.
- Root cause: `Sizable` is typed `Record<string, …>`, so a missing origin type-checks fine and falls back silently. Same class as #6424 (the `credit_card` key missing from seven locales). Suggestion, not tested: type it over the sized origins, e.g. `Record<"string" | "file" | "array" | "set" | "map", …>`, so the next missing key becomes a compile error.
- The `lt` `undefined` suffix is a separate bug in its fallback branch (#6655). Adding `map` to `lt` hides it for maps only.
- I found no existing issue or open PR for this.

`es`, `fr`, `he`, `hr` and `lt` had no `map` entry in `Sizable`, so `z.map()` size errors dropped their unit (`se esperaba que mapa fuera <=1`, and `lt` appended `undefined`). Each now copies its `set` entry, the same convention #6427 used. Hebrew also routes maps through its array/set phrasing ("should contain N items"), taking the verb's gender from its type table.

  z.config(z.locales[l]());
  const m = z.map(z.string(), z.number()).max(1).safeParse(new Map([["a", 1], ["b", 2]])).error.issues[0].message;
  const s = z.set(z.string()).max(1).safeParse(new Set(["a", "b"])).error.issues[0].message;
  console.log(`${l} map: ${m}  |  set: ${s}`);
}
```

fr map: Trop grand : map doit être <=1  |  set: Trop grand : ensemble doit avoir <=1 éléments
he map: גדול מדי: המפה (Map) צריכה להיות <=1  |  set: גדול מדי: הקבוצה (Set) צריכה להכיל 1 פריטים או פחות
hr map: Preveliko: očekivano da mapa bude <=1  |  set: Preveliko: očekivano da skup ima <=1 stavki

A record whose key schema is a constraint — a refine, a regex, a `z.partialRecord` enum — skipped an own `__proto__` input key before the key schema ran, so a JSON body carrying `__proto__` passed records that reject every other bad key. The key now goes through the key schema like any other and is reported as `invalid_key` (or `unrecognized_keys` for a partial enum) when it fails. It is still never written to the output, even when the key schema accepts or renames it, so the stripping from #6386 is unchanged. This matches `.strict()` since #6221 and the exhaustive `z.record(z.enum())` path, which already reported it.

The compiled path gets the same change, and a loose record still drops the key rather than passing it through. Bundle size and record parse throughput are unchanged within noise.

# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Development Commands

Use Nub exclusively for dependency management, scripts, and TypeScript execution. The root `package.json` declares the workspaces and pins Nub; `.nvmrc` selects Node. Nub reads and writes the existing `pnpm-lock.yaml` without requiring pnpm.

Run scripts with `nub run`, repository TypeScript with `nub <file>`, and installed tools with `nub exec --node <tool>`. Keep third-party tools and built-package compatibility probes on plain Node; Nub's augmentation must not mask resolution errors or change test behavior. Use `nub install --frozen-lockfile` for reproducible installs and `nub add` / `nub remove` to manage dependencies.

Key commands:

- `nub run build` - Build all packages (runs recursive build command)
- `nub exec --node vitest run` - Run all tests with Vitest. Includes the compile-mode project, which re-runs the zod tests with global AOT compilation enabled (see `wiki/compile.md`).
- `nub exec --node vitest run <path>` - Run specific test file (e.g., `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/string.test.ts`)
- `nub exec --node vitest run <path> -t "<pattern>"` - Run specific test(s) within a file (e.g., `-t "MAC"`)
- `nub exec --node vitest run --update` - Update all test snapshots
- `nub exec --node vitest run <path> --update` - Update snapshots for specific test file
- `nub run test:watch` - Run tests in watch mode
- `nub exec --node vitest run --coverage` - Run tests with coverage report
- `nub run test:compile` - Focused alias for just the compile-mode project. Already covered by `nub run test`; use this when iterating on compile-related changes.
- `nub run dev` - Execute TypeScript with Nub under source conditions
- `nub run dev <file>` - Execute `<file>` with Nub & proper resolution conditions. Usually use for `play.ts`.
- `nub run dev:play` - Quick alias to run play.ts for experimentation
- `nub run check:comments` - Fail on stacked `//` comment lines (`--fix` joins them)
- `nub run lint` - Run biome linter with auto-fix
- `nub run format` - Format code with biome
- `nub run fix` - Run both format and lint

## Rules

- Nub v0.8.3 and Node.js v24+ required; Nub provisions Node from `.nvmrc`
- ES modules are used throughout (`"type": "module"`)
- All tests must be written in TypeScript - never use JavaScript
- Use `play.ts` for quick experimentation; use proper tests for all permanent test cases
- Features without tests are incomplete - every new feature or bug fix needs test coverage
- Don't skip tests due to type issues - fix the types instead
- Test both success and failure cases with edge cases
- Keep added tests as minimal and dense as possible without sacrificing comprehensiveness; avoid redundant assertions or broad fixtures when a focused case proves the behavior.
- No log statements (`console.log`, `debugger`) in tests or production code
- Never stack prose across consecutive `//` lines. Lines

zod 4.6.5 is affected by CVE-2023-54404

For reference: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2023-54404

zod 4.6.5 is affected by this CVE:

Zod schema-validation library through 4.6.5 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows attackers to exhaust memory by submitting a large array to an application using an array schema without a length constraint. Attackers can exploit the handleArrayResult parse logic in $ZodArray, which accumulates every validation issue for each failing element with no cap or early termination, causing the process to allocate excessive issue objects and crash due to out-of-memory conditions.
description:
`.max()`, `.length()` and `.size()` on arrays, sets and maps now reject an oversized input before any element is parsed. The bound used to run after the walk, so it bounded nothing: `z.array(z.string().uuid()).max(100)` given a million numbers built 1,000,001 issues before it reported `too_big`.

```ts
z.array(z.string().uuid()).max(100).safeParse(Array(1_000_000).fill(0));
// one too_big issue in under a millisecond, was 1,000,001 issues in ~450 ms
```

Only size checks that come before every other check take part, since something like `.overwrite()` can shrink the value first. The early rejection aborts, so a later `.refine()` never sees elements that weren't parsed, and an oversized input reports just the `too_big` issue rather than its element issues too. The compiled path gets the same check ahead of its loop. Unbounded containers are unchanged.

| axis | result |
| --- | --- |
| runtime | The check wraps `parse` only on schemas that carry an upper bound, so an unbounded container runs the same code as before. `z.array(z.string()).max(100)` over 10 items: 65.9 → 67.4 ns (+1–3%, interleaved, but taken at load 10–20). Construction within noise. |
| memory | Unbounded: unchanged. Bounded: +121 B per schema (3421 → 3542) for the wrapper closure. |
| bundle | `zod/mini` array fixture +243 B gzipped (3311 → 3554, +7.3%), +227 with a `maxLength` check. Classic array +215 (+1.0%). Bundles without an array, set or map pay nothing (`zod-mini-object` unchanged). |

Putting the check inside the existing parse closure was smaller (~190 B) but pushed it past V8's inlining budget: `z.array(z.string()).max(n)` parses went 58 → 71 ns.

Fixes #6643

description:
## Summary

Makes `z.config({ jitless: true })` actually silence the Chrome DevTools "Content Security Policy of your site blocks the use of 'eval' in JavaScript" issue on strict-CSP pages, by short-circuiting the `new Function("")` feature probe inside `allowsEval`.

Closes #4461.
Closes #5414.

## Problem

`util.allowsEval` feature-probes for `new Function()` support so the JIT fast-path in `schemas.ts` can be enabled opportunistically. The probe is wrapped in `try/catch`, so it never throws at runtime — **but browsers still log the caught attempt as a `securitypolicyviolation`**, which Chrome surfaces as a Developer Tools Issue:

> Content Security Policy of your site blocks the use of 'eval' in JavaScript

Users on strict CSPs (`script-src` without `'unsafe-eval'`) have flagged this in production error monitors (Datadog, Sentry) — see #5414 where @zbauman3 reported *"literally thousands of errors"* from a single Zod v4 upgrade. The maintainer's documented workaround was:

> ```ts
> z.config({ jitless: true })
> ```

But this doesn't actually help today, because `allowsEval` is memoised via `cached()` and runs lazily on first `.value` access, regardless of whether the user set `jitless` first. Users reported back that setting `jitless` did nothing for the CSP violation, and the thread has stalled.

## Fix

`allowsEval` now consults `globalConfig.jitless` **before** attempting the probe. When `jitless === true`, it returns `false` without invoking `new Function` at all — no CSP violation is ever generated.

```ts
export const allowsEval: { value: boolean } = cached(() => {
  if (globalConfig.jitless) {
    return false;                          // NEW: skip probe entirely
  }
  // @ts-ignore
  if (typeof navigator !== "undefined" && navigator?.userAgent?.includes("Cloudflare")) {
    return false;
  }
  try {
    const F = Function;
    new F("");
    return true;
  } catch (_) {
    return false;
  }
});
```

The change is **minimal, additive, and strictly more restrictive** when opted into. The existing `jit = !core.globalConfig.jitless` gate at `schemas.ts:2025` already routes `jitless=true` users onto the slow path; the probe was just dead weight on their page loads.

## API / behaviour

- **Default unchanged**: when `jitless` is `undefined` (its default), `allowsEval` probes exactly as before — no behaviour shift for the 99% of users who never touch config.
- **Opt-in, safer**: when `jitless=true`, Zod never calls `new Function("")`. Users on strict CSPs now have a clean devtools console.
- **Contract (should be documented)**: `z.config({ jitless: true })` must be called at application entry, before any schema is parsed, because `allowsEval.value` is memoised via `cached()` on first access. Same contract the `jitless` option already implies — this PR doesn't change it.
- **No runtime cost** to users who don't set `jitless` (one extra `if (undefined)` branch on first probe).

## Tests

Added `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts`. It:

1. Calls `z.config({ jitless: true })` at the top of the test.
2. Swaps `globalThis.Function` with a stub that throws if invoked.
3. Asserts `util.allowsEval.value === false`.
4. Asserts the stub was **never called** (the probe really did short-circuit).

The test lives in its own file because vitest isolates ESM graphs per file, so the cached `allowsEval.value` is guaranteed fresh and is never accessed before the config mutation. A `finally` block restores `globalThis.Function` and clears the config flag so other test files in the same worker see the default.

```
✓ src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts (1 test) 2ms
✓ [TS] src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts (1 test)
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
Type Errors no errors
```

## Regression check

Ran the full suite locally (`pnpm test`). All existing tests pass **except** `src/v4/classic/tests/datetime.test.ts > redos checker`, which times out at 5000ms → 13800ms on my Windows/pnpm combo when run under parallel-file concurrency. Isolated run (`pnpm test packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/datetime.test.ts`) passes cleanly in 11.5s / 28 tests. The failure is environmental (ReDoS-check regex timing on a slower machine) and completely unrelated to `util.ts` — same test passes on `main` without this branch. CI on GitHub Actions (Linux) should be clean.

## Scope / risk

- Single file of production change: `packages/zod/src/v4/core/util.ts` (+12 lines, new runtime import + early return).
- One new test file: `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts` (+46 lines).
- No change to public API surface. `$ZodConfig.jitless` already exists on `main` and is documented at `core.ts:129`.
- No dependency changes, no bundler-config changes, no type signature changes.

Happy to iterate on the test style, the comment wording, or split the changelog/docs note into a separate PR if preferred.

## Iterating on a contributor PR in a worktree

When asked to make changes on top of an open PR (e.g. as a maintainer review suggestion), use a worktree so `main` stays clean:

```bash
# 1. Fetch the PR as a local branch and create a worktree for it
git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>
git worktree add ~/.cursor/worktrees/zod/pr-<N> pr-<N>

## Summary

Makes `z.config({ jitless: true })` actually silence the Chrome DevTools "Content Security Policy of your site blocks the use of 'eval' in JavaScript" issue on strict-CSP pages, by short-circuiting the `new Function("")` feature probe inside `allowsEval`.

Closes #4461.
Closes #5414.

## Problem

`util.allowsEval` feature-probes for `new Function()` support so the JIT fast-path in `schemas.ts` can be enabled opportunistically. The probe is wrapped in `try/catch`, so it never throws at runtime — **but browsers still log the caught attempt as a `securitypolicyviolation`**, which Chrome surfaces as a Developer Tools Issue:

> Content Security Policy of your site blocks the use of 'eval' in JavaScript

Users on strict CSPs (`script-src` without `'unsafe-eval'`) have flagged this in production error monitors (Datadog, Sentry) — see #5414 where @zbauman3 reported *"literally thousands of errors"* from a single Zod v4 upgrade. The maintainer's documented workaround was:

> ```ts
> z.config({ jitless: true })
> ```

But this doesn't actually help today, because `allowsEval` is memoised via `cached()` and runs lazily on first `.value` access, regardless of whether the user set `jitless` first. Users reported back that setting `jitless` did nothing for the CSP violation, and the thread has stalled.

## Fix

`allowsEval` now consults `globalConfig.jitless` **before** attempting the probe. When `jitless === true`, it returns `false` without invoking `new Function` at all — no CSP violation is ever generated.

```ts
export const allowsEval: { value: boolean } = cached(() => {
  if (globalConfig.jitless) {
    return false;                          // NEW: skip probe entirely
  }
  // @ts-ignore
  if (typeof navigator !== "undefined" && navigator?.userAgent?.includes("Cloudflare")) {
    return false;
  }
  try {
    const F = Function;
    new F("");
    return true;
  } catch (_) {
    return false;
  }
});
```

The change is **minimal, additive, and strictly more restrictive** when opted into. The existing `jit = !core.globalConfig.jitless` gate at `schemas.ts:2025` already routes `jitless=true` users onto the slow path; the probe was just dead weight on their page loads.

## API / behaviour

- **Default unchanged**: when `jitless` is `undefined` (its default), `allowsEval` probes exactly as before — no behaviour shift for the 99% of users who never touch config.
- **Opt-in, safer**: when `jitless=true`, Zod never calls `new Function("")`. Users on strict CSPs now have a clean devtools console.
- **Contract (should be documented)**: `z.config({ jitless: true })` must be called at application entry, before any schema is parsed, because `allowsEval.value` is memoised via `cached()` on first access. Same contract the `jitless` option already implies — this PR doesn't change it.
- **No runtime cost** to users who don't set `jitless` (one extra `if (undefined)` branch on first probe).

## Tests

Added `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts`. It:

1. Calls `z.config({ jitless: true })` at the top of the test.
2. Swaps `globalThis.Function` with a stub that throws if invoked.
3. Asserts `util.allowsEval.value === false`.
4. Asserts the stub was **never called** (the probe really did short-circuit).

The test lives in its own file because vitest isolates ESM graphs per file, so the cached `allowsEval.value` is guaranteed fresh and is never accessed before the config mutation. A `finally` block restores `globalThis.Function` and clears the config flag so other test files in the same worker see the default.

```
✓ src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts (1 test) 2ms
✓ [TS] src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts (1 test)
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
Type Errors no errors
```

## Regression check

Ran the full suite locally (`pnpm test`). All existing tests pass **except** `src/v4/classic/tests/datetime.test.ts > redos checker`, which times out at 5000ms → 13800ms on my Windows/pnpm combo when run under parallel-file concurrency. Isolated run (`pnpm test packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/datetime.test.ts`) passes cleanly in 11.5s / 28 tests. The failure is environmental (ReDoS-check regex timing on a slower machine) and completely unrelated to `util.ts` — same test passes on `main` without this branch. CI on GitHub Actions (Linux) should be clean.

## Scope / risk

- Single file of production change: `packages/zod/src/v4/core/util.ts` (+12 lines, new runtime import + early return).
- One new test file: `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts` (+46 lines).
- No change to public API surface. `$ZodConfig.jitless` already exists on `main` and is documented at `core.ts:129`.
- No dependency changes, no bundler-config changes, no type signature changes.

Happy to iterate on the test style, the comment wording, or split the changelog/docs note into a separate PR if preferred.

## Summary

Makes `z.config({ jitless: true })` actually silence the Chrome DevTools "Content Security Policy of your site blocks the use of 'eval' in JavaScript" issue on strict-CSP pages, by short-circuiting the `new Function("")` feature probe inside `allowsEval`.

Closes #4461.
Closes #5414.

## Problem

`util.allowsEval` feature-probes for `new Function()` support so the JIT fast-path in `schemas.ts` can be enabled opportunistically. The probe is wrapped in `try/catch`, so it never throws at runtime — **but browsers still log the caught attempt as a `securitypolicyviolation`**, which Chrome surfaces as a Developer Tools Issue:

> Content Security Policy of your site blocks the use of 'eval' in JavaScript

Users on strict CSPs (`script-src` without `'unsafe-eval'`) have flagged this in production error monitors (Datadog, Sentry) — see #5414 where @zbauman3 reported *"literally thousands of errors"* from a single Zod v4 upgrade. The maintainer's documented workaround was:

> ```ts
> z.config({ jitless: true })
> ```

But this doesn't actually help today, because `allowsEval` is memoised via `cached()` and runs lazily on first `.value` access, regardless of whether the user set `jitless` first. Users reported back that setting `jitless` did nothing for the CSP violation, and the thread has stalled.

## Fix

`allowsEval` now consults `globalConfig.jitless` **before** attempting the probe. When `jitless === true`, it returns `false` without invoking `new Function` at all — no CSP violation is ever generated.

```ts
export const allowsEval: { value: boolean } = cached(() => {
  if (globalConfig.jitless) {
    return false;                          // NEW: skip probe entirely
  }
  // @ts-ignore
  if (typeof navigator !== "undefined" && navigator?.userAgent?.includes("Cloudflare")) {
    return false;
  }
  try {
    const F = Function;
    new F("");
    return true;
  } catch (_) {
    return false;
  }
});
```

The change is **minimal, additive, and strictly more restrictive** when opted into. The existing `jit = !core.globalConfig.jitless` gate at `schemas.ts:2025` already routes `jitless=true` users onto the slow path; the probe was just dead weight on their page loads.

- **Default unchanged**: when `jitless` is `undefined` (its default), `allowsEval` probes exactly as before — no behaviour shift for the 99% of users who never touch config.
- **Opt-in, safer**: when `jitless=true`, Zod never calls `new Function("")`. Users on strict CSPs now have a clean devtools console.
- **Contract (should be documented)**: `z.config({ jitless: true })` must be called at application entry, before any schema is parsed, because `allowsEval.value` is memoised via `cached()` on first access. Same contract the `jitless` option already implies — this PR doesn't change it.
- **No runtime cost** to users who don't set `jitless` (one extra `if (undefined)` branch on first probe).

## Tests

Added `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/jitless-allows-eval.test.ts`. It:

2. Swaps `globalThis.Function` with a stub that throws if invoked.
3. Asserts `util.allowsEval.value === false`.
4. Asserts the stub was **never called** (the probe really did short-circuit).

The test lives in its own file because vitest isolates ESM graphs per file, so the cached `allowsEval.value` is guaranteed fresh and is never accessed before the config mutation. mount() middleware cuts the wrong path prefix when the route has a parameter

### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.13

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Node.js 22 (also reproducible with app.request, so runtime independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The mount() middleware rewrites the request path before passing it to the mounted app. The default replaceRequest uses routePath(c), which is the registered route pattern. When the pattern contains a parameter segment, the pattern length no longer matches the real matched prefix, so the wrong slice of the path is removed.

Reproduction:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { mount } from 'hono/mount'

const sub = new Hono()
sub.get('/hello', (c) => c.text('sub sees: ' + c.req.path))

const app = new Hono()
app.all('/api/:version/*', mount(sub.fetch))

const res = await app.request('/api/v1/hello')
console.log(await res.text())
```

routePath(c) is "/api/:version/*", so pathPrefix becomes "/api/:version" (13 chars). c.req.path is "/api/v1/hello", also 13 chars, so the slice removes everything and the sub app receives "/". With a longer remainder the cut lands in the middle of the remaining path. Regex params such as /r/:id{[0-9]+}/* behave the same way.

### What is the expected behavior?

The concrete matched prefix (/api/v1) should be stripped, so the mounted app receives /hello. Mounting on /api/v1 with no remainder should map to /.

### What do you see instead?

The mounted app receives "/" for /api/v1/hello, because the route pattern text is measured instead of the matched prefix. Fixed prefixes (like /api/*) work fine since the pattern and the matched prefix have the same length there.

### Additional information

I have a fix ready that resolves the concrete prefix by walking the route pattern segments and consuming one path segment per parameter, with tests covering param, regex param and encoded paths. I will open a PR that references this issue.
description:
fixes #5546

This PR resolves dynamic prefixes using the request path and the router’s captured parameter values. It also handles intermediate wildcards, including patterns such as `/x*/y/*`.

Although callers can work around this with `replaceRequest`, I think this is a case that `mount()` should handle by default. Since `mount()` was recently extracted from core into middleware, the additional code seems reasonable.

The implementation accesses the internal match result to obtain parameter values before `param()` decodes them. Those values are needed to calculate the correct offsets in the request path. This introduces a dependency on internal structures, but I think that is acceptable for middleware shipped with Hono.

### Duplicate parameter names

The default request rewriting now throws an error at runtime if the mount route contains duplicate parameter names. The router’s match result identifies captured values by parameter name, so duplicate names cannot be resolved reliably when calculating the prefix length. The error includes the duplicate name and the route.

### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `pnpm run check:fix` to format and lint the code

# Contribution Guide

Contributions Welcome! We will be glad for your help.
You can contribute in the following ways.

- Create an Issue - Propose a new feature. Report a bug.
- Build middleware and libraries - Grow the Hono ecosystem.
- Share - Share your thoughts on the Blog, X, and others.
- Sponsor - Support the maintainers through GitHub Sponsors: [@yusukebe](https://github.com/sponsors/yusukebe) and [@usualoma](https://github.com/sponsors/usualoma).
- Make your application - Please try to use Hono.

Note:
This project is started by Yusuke Wada ([@yusukebe](https://github.com/yusukebe)) for the hobby proposal.
It was just for fun. For now, this stance has not been changed basically.
I want to write the code as I like.
So, if you propose great ideas, but I do not appropriate them, the idea may not be accepted.

Although, don't worry!
Hono is tested well, polished by the contributors, and used by many developers. And I'll try my best to make Hono cool and hot, beautiful, and ultrafast.

## AI Usage Policy

You may use AI to contribute, but it must never waste a maintainer's time or make their work unpleasant.

To enforce this, and regardless of whether AI was actually used, a maintainer may close your issue without notice and block your account.

## Issues instead of Pull Requests

Pull requests are limited to maintainers. If you find a bug or want a change, please create an issue instead. A clear issue with a minimal reproduction helps us more than a pull request.

If you have already fixed it in your fork, you can link the branch in the issue. A maintainer may open a pull request from it, and your commits keep your name.

## Local Development

The `honojs/hono` project uses [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) as its package manager, and [Bun](https://bun.sh/) to run the build and some of the tests. Developers should install both.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

task:
mount() middleware cuts the wrong path prefix when the route has a parameter

### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.13

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Node.js 22 (also reproducible with app.request, so runtime independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The mount() middleware rewrites the request path before passing it to the mounted app. The default replaceRequest uses routePath(c), which is the registered route pattern. When the pattern contains a parameter segment, the pattern length no longer matches the real matched prefix, so the wrong slice of the path is removed.

Reproduction:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { mount } from 'hono/mount'

const sub = new Hono()
sub.get('/hello', (c) => c.text('sub sees: ' + c.req.path))

const app = new Hono()
app.all('/api/:version/*', mount(sub.fetch))

const res = await app.request('/api/v1/hello')
console.log(await res.text())
```

routePath(c) is "/api/:version/*", so pathPrefix becomes "/api/:version" (13 chars). c.req.path is "/api/v1/hello", also 13 chars, so the slice removes everything and the sub app receives "/". With a longer remainder the cut lands in the middle of the remaining path. Regex params such as /r/:id{[0-9]+}/* behave the same way.

### What is the expected behavior?

The concrete matched prefix (/api/v1) should be stripped, so the mounted app receives /hello. Mounting on /api/v1 with no remainder should map to /.

### What do you see instead?

The mounted app receives "/" for /api/v1/hello, because the route pattern text is measured instead of the matched prefix. Fixed prefixes (like /api/*) work fine since the pattern and the matched prefix have the same length there.

### Additional information

I have a fix ready that resolves the concrete prefix by walking the route pattern segments and consuming one path segment per parameter, with tests covering param, regex param and encoded paths. I will open a PR that references this issue.
description:
fixes #5546

This PR resolves dynamic prefixes using the request path and the router’s captured parameter values. It also handles intermediate wildcards, including patterns such as `/x*/y/*`.

Although callers can work around this with `replaceRequest`, I think this is a case that `mount()` should handle by default. Since `mount()` was recently extracted from core into middleware, the additional code seems reasonable.

The implementation accesses the internal match result to obtain parameter values before `param()` decodes them. Those values are needed to calculate the correct offsets in the request path. This introduces a dependency on internal structures, but I think that is acceptable for middleware shipped with Hono.

### Duplicate parameter names

The default request rewriting now throws an error at runtime if the mount route contains duplicate parameter names. The router’s match result identifies captured values by parameter name, so duplicate names cannot be resolved reliably when calculating the prefix length. The error includes the duplicate name and the route.

### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `pnpm run check:fix` to format and lint the code

task:
mount() middleware cuts the wrong path prefix when the route has a parameter

### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.13

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Node.js 22 (also reproducible with app.request, so runtime independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The mount() middleware rewrites the request path before passing it to the mounted app. The default replaceRequest uses routePath(c), which is the registered route pattern. When the pattern contains a parameter segment, the pattern length no longer matches the real matched prefix, so the wrong slice of the path is removed.

Reproduction:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { mount } from 'hono/mount'

const sub = new Hono()
sub.get('/hello', (c) => c.text('sub sees: ' + c.req.path))

const app = new Hono()
app.all('/api/:version/*', mount(sub.fetch))

const res = await app.request('/api/v1/hello')
console.log(await res.text())
```

routePath(c) is "/api/:version/*", so pathPrefix becomes "/api/:version" (13 chars). c.req.path is "/api/v1/hello", also 13 chars, so the slice removes everything and the sub app receives "/". With a longer remainder the cut lands in the middle of the remaining path. Regex params such as /r/:id{[0-9]+}/* behave the same way.

### What is the expected behavior?

The concrete matched prefix (/api/v1) should be stripped, so the mounted app receives /hello. Mounting on /api/v1 with no remainder should map to /.

### What do you see instead?

The mounted app receives "/" for /api/v1/hello, because the route pattern text is measured instead of the matched prefix. Fixed prefixes (like /api/*) work fine since the pattern and the matched prefix have the same length there.

### Additional information

I have a fix ready that resolves the concrete prefix by walking the route pattern segments and consuming one path segment per parameter, with tests covering param, regex param and encoded paths. I will open a PR that references this issue.
description:
fixes #5546

This PR resolves dynamic prefixes using the request path and the router’s captured parameter values. It also handles intermediate wildcards, including patterns such as `/x*/y/*`.

Although callers can work around this with `replaceRequest`, I think this is a case that `mount()` should handle by default. Since `mount()` was recently extracted from core into middleware, the additional code seems reasonable.

The implementation accesses the internal match result to obtain parameter values before `param()` decodes them. Those values are needed to calculate the correct offsets in the request path. This introduces a dependency on internal structures, but I think that is acceptable for middleware shipped with Hono.

### Duplicate parameter names

The default request rewriting now throws an error at runtime if the mount route contains duplicate parameter names. The router’s match result identifies captured values by parameter name, so duplicate names cannot be resolved reliably when calculating the prefix length. The error includes the duplicate name and the route.

### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `pnpm run check:fix` to format and lint the code

task:
mount() middleware cuts the wrong path prefix when the route has a parameter

### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.13

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Node.js 22 (also reproducible with app.request, so runtime independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The mount() middleware rewrites the request path before passing it to the mounted app. The default replaceRequest uses routePath(c), which is the registered route pattern. When the pattern contains a parameter segment, the pattern length no longer matches the real matched prefix, so the wrong slice of the path is removed.

Reproduction:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { mount } from 'hono/mount'

const sub = new Hono()
sub.get('/hello', (c) => c.text('sub sees: ' + c.req.path))

const app = new Hono()
app.all('/api/:version/*', mount(sub.fetch))

const res = await app.request('/api/v1/hello')
console.log(await res.text())
```

routePath(c) is "/api/:version/*", so pathPrefix becomes "/api/:version" (13 chars). c.req.path is "/api/v1/hello", also 13 chars, so the slice removes everything and the sub app receives "/". With a longer remainder the cut lands in the middle of the remaining path. Regex params such as /r/:id{[0-9]+}/* behave the same way.

### What is the expected behavior?

The concrete matched prefix (/api/v1) should be stripped, so the mounted app receives /hello. Mounting on /api/v1 with no remainder should map to /.

### What do you see instead?

The mounted app receives "/" for /api/v1/hello, because the route pattern text is measured instead of the matched prefix. Fixed prefixes (like /api/*) work fine since the pattern and the matched prefix have the same length there.

### Additional information

I have a fix ready that resolves the concrete prefix by walking the route pattern segments and consuming one path segment per parameter, with tests covering param, regex param and encoded paths. I will open a PR that references this issue.
description:
fixes #5546

This PR resolves dynamic prefixes using the request path and the router’s captured parameter values. It also handles intermediate wildcards, including patterns such as `/x*/y/*`.

Although callers can work around this with `replaceRequest`, I think this is a case that `mount()` should handle by default. Since `mount()` was recently extracted from core into middleware, the additional code seems reasonable.

The implementation accesses the internal match result to obtain parameter values before `param()` decodes them. Those values are needed to calculate the correct offsets in the request path. This introduces a dependency on internal structures, but I think that is acceptable for middleware shipped with Hono.

### Duplicate parameter names

The default request rewriting now throws an error at runtime if the mount route contains duplicate parameter names. The router’s match result identifies captured values by parameter name, so duplicate names cannot be resolved reliably when calculating the prefix length. The error includes the duplicate name and the route.

### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `pnpm run check:fix` to format and lint the code

mount() middleware cuts the wrong path prefix when the route has a parameter

### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.13

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Node.js 22 (also reproducible with app.request, so runtime independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The mount() middleware rewrites the request path before passing it to the mounted app. The default replaceRequest uses routePath(c), which is the registered route pattern. When the pattern contains a parameter segment, the pattern length no longer matches the real matched prefix, so the wrong slice of the path is removed.

Reproduction:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { mount } from 'hono/mount'

const sub = new Hono()
sub.get('/hello', (c) => c.text('sub sees: ' + c.req.path))

const app = new Hono()
app.all('/api/:version/*', mount(sub.fetch))

const res = await app.request('/api/v1/hello')
console.log(await res.text())
```

routePath(c) is "/api/:version/*", so pathPrefix becomes "/api/:version" (13 chars). c.req.path is "/api/v1/hello", also 13 chars, so the slice removes everything and the sub app receives "/". With a longer remainder the cut lands in the middle of the remaining path. Regex params such as /r/:id{[0-9]+}/* behave the same way.

### What is the expected behavior?

The concrete matched prefix (/api/v1) should be stripped, so the mounted app receives /hello. Mounting on /api/v1 with no remainder should map to /.

### What do you see instead?

The mounted app receives "/" for /api/v1/hello, because the route pattern text is measured instead of the matched prefix. Fixed prefixes (like /api/*) work fine since the pattern and the matched prefix have the same length there.

### Additional information

I have a fix ready that resolves the concrete prefix by walking the route pattern segments and consuming one path segment per parameter, with tests covering param, regex param and encoded paths. I will open a PR that references this issue.

description:
fixes #5546

This PR resolves dynamic prefixes using the request path and the router’s captured parameter values. It also handles intermediate wildcards, including patterns such as `/x*/y/*`.

Although callers can work around this with `replaceRequest`, I think this is a case that `mount()` should handle by default. Since `mount()` was recently extracted from core into middleware, the additional code seems reasonable.

The implementation accesses the internal match result to obtain parameter values before `param()` decodes them. Those values are needed to calculate the correct offsets in the request path. This introduces a dependency on internal structures, but I think that is acceptable for middleware shipped with Hono.

### Duplicate parameter names

The default request rewriting now throws an error at runtime if the mount route contains duplicate parameter names. The router’s match result identifies captured values by parameter name, so duplicate names cannot be resolved reliably when calculating the prefix length. The error includes the duplicate name and the route.

### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `pnpm run check:fix` to format and lint the code

fix(css): Fix multiline CSS handling in style replacement

## Summary

Fix an issue where `Style` fails to append generated CSS when the existing `<style>` element contains a newline.

## Reproduction

The following works as expected:

```tsx
<Style>{css`/* comment（コメントが１行ならOK！） */`}</Style>
```

However, adding a newline inside the comment causes the generated CSS not to be appended:

```tsx
<Style>{css`
/* comment
コメントが複数行に渡る場合、おそらく改行が残るためNG?
another line */
`}</Style>
```

This also occurs with multiline comments in otherwise valid CSS.

## Cause

The style replacement regex currently uses `.*?`:

```ts
const replaceStyleRe = new RegExp(
  `(<style id="${id}"(?: nonce="[^"]*")?>.*?)(</style>)`
)
```

In JavaScript regular expressions, `.` does not match line terminators by default. Therefore, the expression cannot match the complete `<style>` element when its contents contain a newline.

## Fix

Use `[\s\S]*?` instead of `.*?` so that multiline style contents are matched:

```diff
- const replaceStyleRe = new RegExp(`(<style id="${id}"(?: nonce="[^"]*")?>.*?)(</style>)`)
+ const replaceStyleRe = new RegExp(`(<style id="${id}"(?: nonce="[^"]*")?>[\\s\\S]*?)(</style>)`)
```

This allows the existing style contents to be matched regardless of line breaks.

The following works as expected:

```tsx
<Style>{css`/* comment（コメントが１行ならOK！） */`}</Style>
```

However, adding a newline inside the comment causes the generated CSS not to be appended:

```tsx
<Style>{css`
/* comment
コメントが複数行に渡る場合、おそらく改行が残るためNG?
another line */
`}</Style>
```

This also occurs with multiline comments in otherwise valid CSS.

## Cause

The style replacement regex currently uses `.*?`:

```ts
const replaceStyleRe = new RegExp(
  `(<style id="${id}"(?: nonce="[^"]*")?>.*?)(</style>)`
)
```

In JavaScript regular expressions, `.` does not match line terminators by default. Therefore, the expression cannot match the complete `<style>` element when its contents contain a newline.

## Fix

Use `[\s\S]*?` instead of `.*?` so that multiline style contents are matched:

```diff
- const replaceStyleRe = new RegExp(`(<style id="${id}"(?: nonce="[^"]*")?>.*?)(</style>)`)
+ const replaceStyleRe = new RegExp(`(<style id="${id}"(?: nonce="[^"]*")?>[\\s\\S]*?)(</style>)`)
```

This allows the existing style contents to be matched regardless of line breaks.

# Contribution Guide

Contributions Welcome! We will be glad for your help.
You can contribute in the following ways.

- Create an Issue - Propose a new feature. Report a bug.
- Pull Request - Fix a bug or typo. Refactor the code.
- Create third-party middleware - See instructions below.
- Share - Share your thoughts on the Blog, X, and others.
- Make your application - Please try to use Hono.

Note:
This project is started by Yusuke Wada ([@yusukebe](https://github.com/yusukebe)) for the hobby proposal.
It was just for fun. For now, this stance has not been changed basically.
I want to write the code as I like.
So, if you propose great ideas, but I do not appropriate them, the idea may not be accepted.

Although, don't worry!
Hono is tested well, polished by the contributors, and used by many developers. And I'll try my best to make Hono cool and hot, beautiful, and ultrafast.

## AI Usage Policy

You may use AI to contribute, but it must never waste a maintainer's time or make their work unpleasant.

To enforce this, and regardless of whether AI was actually used, a maintainer may close your PR without notice and block your account.

## Installing dependencies

The `honojs/hono` project uses [Bun](https://bun.sh/) as its package manager. Developers should install Bun.

After that, please install the dependency environment.

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

## PRs

Please ensure your PR passes tests with `bun run test`.

## Third-party middleware

Third-party middleware is not in the core.
It is allowed to depend on other libraries or work only in specific environments, such as Cloudflare Workers. For example:

- GraphQL Server middleware
- Firebase Auth middleware
- Sentry middleware

You can make a third-party middleware by yourself.
It may be under the "honojs organization" and distributed in the `@honojs` namespace.

The monorepo "[honojs/middleware](https://github.com/honojs/middleware)" manages these middleware.
If you want to do it, create an issue about your middleware.

## Local Development

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

/**
 * @module
 * This module is the base module for the Hono object.
 */

/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any */
import { compose } from './compose'
import { Context } from './context'
import type { ExecutionContext } from './context'
import type { Router } from './router'
import { METHODS, METHOD_NAME_ALL, METHOD_NAME_ALL_LOWERCASE } from './router'
import type {
  Env,
  ErrorHandler,
  FetchEventLike,
  H,
  HandlerInterface,
  MergePath,
  MergeSchemaPath,
  MiddlewareHandler,
  MiddlewareHandlerInterface,
  Next,
  NotFoundHandler,
  OnHandlerInterface,
  RouterRoute,
  Schema,
} from './types'
import { COMPOSED_HANDLER } from './utils/constants'
import { getPath, getPathNoStrict, mergePath } from './utils/url'

const notFoundHandler: NotFoundHandler = (c) => {
  return c.text('404 Not Found', 404)
}

const errorHandler: ErrorHandler = (err, c) => {
  if ('getResponse' in err) {
    const res = err.getResponse()
    return c.newResponse(res.body, res)
  }
  console.error(err)
  return c.text('Internal Server Error', 500)
}

type GetPath<E extends Env> = (request: Request, options?: { env?: E['Bindings'] }) => string

export type HonoOptions<E extends Env> = {
  /**
   * `router` option specifies which router to use.
   *
   * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/hono#router-option}
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * const app = new Hono({ router: new RegExpRouter() })
   * ```
   */
  router?: Router<[H, RouterRoute]>
} & (
  | {
      /**
       * `strict` option specifies whether to distinguish whether the last path is a directory or not.
       *
       * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/hono#strict-mode}
       *
       * @default true
       */
      strict?: true
      /**
       * `getPath` can handle the host header value.
       *
       * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/routing#routing-with-host-header-value}
       *
       * @example
       * ```ts
       * const app = new Hono({
       *  getPath: (req) =>
       *   '/' + req.headers.get('host') + req.url.replace(/^https?:\/\/[^/]+(\/[^?]*)/, '$1'),
       * })
       *
       * app.get('/www1.example.com/hello', () => c.text('hello www1'))
       *
       * // A following request will match the route:
       * // new Request('http://www1.example.com/hello', {
       * //  headers: { host: 'www1.example.com' },
       * // })
       * ```
       */
      getPath?: GetPath<E>
    }
  | {
      /**
       * `strict` option specifies whether to distinguish whether the last path is a directory or not.
       * When `strict` is `false`, `getPath` is not used.
       *
       * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/hono#strict-mode}
       *
       * @default true
       */
      strict: false
      getPath?: never
    }
)

type MountOptionHandler = (c: Context) => unknown
type MountReplaceRequest = (originalRequest: Request) => Request
type MountOptions =
  | MountOptionHandler
  | {
      optionHandler?: MountOptionHandler
      replaceRequest?: MountReplaceRequest | false
    }

class Hono<
  E extends Env = Env,
  S extends Schema = {},
  BasePath extends string = '/',
  CurrentPath extends string = BasePath,
> {
  get!: HandlerInterface<E, 'get', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  post!: HandlerInterface<E, 'post', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  put!: HandlerInterface<E, 'put', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  delete!: HandlerInterface<E, 'delete', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  options!: HandlerInterface<E, 'options', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  patch!: HandlerInterface<E, 'patch', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  query!: HandlerInterface<E, 'query', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  all!: HandlerInterface<E, 'all', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  on: OnHandlerInterface<E, S, BasePath>
  use: MiddlewareHandlerInterface<E, S, BasePath>

  /*
    This class is like an abstract class and does not have a router.
    To use it, inherit the class and implement router in the constructor.

/**
 * @module
 * This module is the base module for the Hono object.
 */

/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any */
import { compose } from './compose'
import { Context } from './context'
import type { ExecutionContext } from './context'
import type { Router } from './router'
import { METHODS, METHOD_NAME_ALL, METHOD_NAME_ALL_LOWERCASE } from './router'
import type {
  Env,
  ErrorHandler,
  FetchEventLike,
  H,
  HandlerInterface,
  MergePath,
  MergeSchemaPath,
  MiddlewareHandler,
  MiddlewareHandlerInterface,
  Next,
  NotFoundHandler,
  OnHandlerInterface,
  RouterRoute,
  Schema,
} from './types'
import { COMPOSED_HANDLER } from './utils/constants'
import { getPath, getPathNoStrict, mergePath } from './utils/url'

const notFoundHandler: NotFoundHandler = (c) => {
  return c.text('404 Not Found', 404)
}

const errorHandler: ErrorHandler = (err, c) => {
  if ('getResponse' in err) {
    const res = err.getResponse()
    return c.newResponse(res.body, res)
  }
  console.error(err)
  return c.text('Internal Server Error', 500)
}

type GetPath<E extends Env> = (request: Request, options?: { env?: E['Bindings'] }) => string

export type HonoOptions<E extends Env> = {
  /**
   * `router` option specifies which router to use.
   *
   * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/hono#router-option}
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * const app = new Hono({ router: new RegExpRouter() })
   * ```
   */
  router?: Router<[H, RouterRoute]>
} & (
  | {
      /**
       * `strict` option specifies whether to distinguish whether the last path is a directory or not.
       *
       * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/hono#strict-mode}
       *
       * @default true
       */
      strict?: true
      /**
       * `getPath` can handle the host header value.
       *
       * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/routing#routing-with-host-header-value}
       *
       * @example
       * ```ts
       * const app = new Hono({
       *  getPath: (req) =>
       *   '/' + req.headers.get('host') + req.url.replace(/^https?:\/\/[^/]+(\/[^?]*)/, '$1'),
       * })
       *
       * app.get('/www1.example.com/hello', () => c.text('hello www1'))
       *
       * // A following request will match the route:
       * // new Request('http://www1.example.com/hello', {
       * //  headers: { host: 'www1.example.com' },
       * // })
       * ```
       */
      getPath?: GetPath<E>
    }
  | {
      /**
       * `strict` option specifies whether to distinguish whether the last path is a directory or not.
       * When `strict` is `false`, `getPath` is not used.
       *
       * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/hono#strict-mode}
       *
       * @default true
       */
      strict: false
      getPath?: never
    }
)

type MountOptionHandler = (c: Context) => unknown
type MountReplaceRequest = (originalRequest: Request) => Request
type MountOptions =
  | MountOptionHandler
  | {
      optionHandler?: MountOptionHandler
      replaceRequest?: MountReplaceRequest | false
    }

class Hono<
  E extends Env = Env,
  S extends Schema = {},
  BasePath extends string = '/',
  CurrentPath extends string = BasePath,
> {
  get!: HandlerInterface<E, 'get', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  post!: HandlerInterface<E, 'post', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  put!: HandlerInterface<E, 'put', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  delete!: HandlerInterface<E, 'delete', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>

  patch!: HandlerInterface<E, 'patch', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  query!: HandlerInterface<E, 'query', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  all!: HandlerInterface<E, 'all', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
  on: OnHandlerInterface<E, S, BasePath>
  use: MiddlewareHandlerInterface<E, S, BasePath>

  /*
    This class is like an abstract class and does not have a router.
    To use it, inherit the class and implement router in the constructor.
  */
  router!: Router<[H, RouterRoute]>

[docs/CONTRIBUTING.md]
# Contribution Guide

Contributions Welcome! We will be glad for your help.
You can contribute in the following ways.

- Create an Issue - Propose a new feature. Report a bug.
- Build middleware and libraries - Grow the Hono ecosystem.
- Share - Share your thoughts on the Blog, X, and others.
- Sponsor - Support the maintainers through GitHub Sponsors: [@yusukebe](https://github.com/sponsors/yusukebe) and [@usualoma](https://github.com/sponsors/usualoma).
- Make your application - Please try to use Hono.

Note:
This project is started by Yusuke Wada ([@yusukebe](https://github.com/yusukebe)) for the hobby proposal.
It was just for fun. For now, this stance has not been changed basically.
I want to write the code as I like.
So, if you propose great ideas, but I do not appropriate them, the idea may not be accepted.

Although, don't worry!
Hono is tested well, polished by the contributors, and used by many developers. And I'll try my best to make Hono cool and hot, beautiful, and ultrafast.

## AI Usage Policy

You may use AI to contribute, but it must never waste a maintainer's time or make their work unpleasant.

To enforce this, and regardless of whether AI was actually used, a maintainer may close your issue without notice and block your account.

## Issues instead of Pull Requests

Pull requests are limited to maintainers. If you find a bug or want a change, please create an issue instead. A clear issue with a minimal reproduction helps us more than a pull request.

If you have already fixed it in your fork, you can link the branch in the issue. A maintainer may open a pull request from it, and your commits keep your name.

## Local Development

The `honojs/hono` project uses [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) as its package manager, and [Bun](https://bun.sh/) to run the build and some of the tests. Developers should install both.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

# Contribution Guide

Contributions Welcome! We will be glad for your help.
You can contribute in the following ways.

- Create an Issue - Propose a new feature. Report a bug.
- Build middleware and libraries - Grow the Hono ecosystem.
- Share - Share your thoughts on the Blog, X, and others.

So, if you propose great ideas, but I do not appropriate them, the idea may not be accepted.

Although, don't worry!

You may use AI to contribute, but it must never waste a maintainer's time or make their work unpleasant.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

[docs/CONTRIBUTING.md]
# Contribution Guide

Contributions Welcome! We will be glad for your help.
You can contribute in the following ways.

- Create an Issue - Propose a new feature. Report a bug.
- Build middleware and libraries - Grow the Hono ecosystem.
- Share - Share your thoughts on the Blog, X, and others.
- Sponsor - Support the maintainers through GitHub Sponsors: [@yusukebe](https://github.com/sponsors/yusukebe) and [@usualoma](https://github.com/sponsors/usualoma).
- Make your application - Please try to use Hono.

Note:
This project is started by Yusuke Wada ([@yusukebe](https://github.com/yusukebe)) for the hobby proposal.
It was just for fun. For now, this stance has not been changed basically.
I want to write the code as I like.
So, if you propose great ideas, but I do not appropriate them, the idea may not be accepted.

Although, don't worry!
Hono is tested well, polished by the contributors, and used by many developers. And I'll try my best to make Hono cool and hot, beautiful, and ultrafast.

## AI Usage Policy

You may use AI to contribute, but it must never waste a maintainer's time or make their work unpleasant.

To enforce this, and regardless of whether AI was actually used, a maintainer may close your issue without notice and block your account.

## Issues instead of Pull Requests

Pull requests are limited to maintainers. If you find a bug or want a change, please create an issue instead. A clear issue with a minimal reproduction helps us more than a pull request.

If you have already fixed it in your fork, you can link the branch in the issue. A maintainer may open a pull request from it, and your commits keep your name.

## Local Development

The `honojs/hono` project uses [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) as its package manager, and [Bun](https://bun.sh/) to run the build and some of the tests. Developers should install both.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

Adding an unrelated route can change duplicate path parameter values

### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.8. Also reproduced on current main (52febbcc).

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Node.js 25.2.1

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Both apps declare the same route and receive the same request. The second one only adds an unrelated `/a`.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { getRouterName } from 'hono/dev'

const a = new Hono()
a.get('/:id/:id/x', (c) => c.text(c.req.param('id')))
const resA = await a.request('/123/456/x')
console.log(await resA.text()) // 123
console.log(getRouterName(a))  // SmartRouter + RegExpRouter

const b = new Hono()
b.get('/:id/:id/x', (c) => c.text(c.req.param('id')))
b.get('/a', (c) => c.text('a'))
const resB = await b.request('/123/456/x')
console.log(await resB.text()) // 456
console.log(getRouterName(b))  // SmartRouter + TrieRouter
```

The request never reaches `/a`, but adding that route changes what `c.req.param('id')` returns.

### What is the expected behavior?

`c.req.param('id')` should not depend on which router `SmartRouter` picks.

In #1566 the first value was chosen when the same parameter name appears more than once in a path, and the shared router test still asserts it for `/:id/:id`:

```ts
it('self', () => {
  router.add('GET', '/:id/:id', 'foo')
  const res = match('GET', '/123/456')
  expect(res[0].params['id']).toBe('123')
})
```

### What do you see instead?

For `/:id/:id` and `/123/456`, `RegExpRouter`, `TrieRouter` and `LinearRouter` all return `123`. For `/:id/:id/x` and `/123/456/x`, `TrieRouter` returns `456` while the other two still return `123`.

With `/:id/:id/:id` and `/1/2/3` `TrieRouter` returns `2`, so it is not taking the last value either.

Under the default `SmartRouter`, adding `/a` switches the selection from `RegExpRouter` to `TrieRouter`, so the same request to the same route returns a different parameter value.

### Additional information

I traced this to `TrieRouter`. For `/:id/:id/x` the duplicate `id` gets overwritten while traversing the trie, and the two-segment case is handled differently in the final matching step.

That seems to be why `/:id/:id` returns `123` but `/:id/:id/x` returns `456`.

## Summary

Fixes #5422.

`TrieRouter` did not consistently keep the **first** value when the same path parameter name appeared more than once (e.g. `/:id/:id/x`). `RegExpRouter` / `LinearRouter` already follow first-wins, and `src/router/common.case.test.ts` asserts that for `/:id/:id`. For longer paths the trie overwrite left a different value, so `SmartRouter` could change `c.req.param('id')` merely by registering an unrelated route that switches the selected router.

### Root cause

In `src/router/trie-router/node.ts`, `search()` assigned `params[name] = part` (and the regexp-matcher equivalent), overwriting earlier values for the same name. That made `/:id/:id/x` return the second segment and `/:id/:id/:id` return the middle one.

### Fix

Record a path param only if that name is not already an own property (`Object.hasOwn`). Nullish assignment (`??=`) alone is not enough because a normal `{}` already has `constructor` on the prototype (caught by the reserved-words suite).

Tests extended in shared router cases, TrieRouter node tests, and a SmartRouter/`Hono` integration case that matches the issue reproduction.

Assisted by AI tooling; changes and tests were reviewed and verified against the failing reproduction from #5422.

# Contribution Guide

Contributions Welcome! We will be glad for your help.
You can contribute in the following ways.

- Create an Issue - Propose a new feature. Report a bug.
- Pull Request - Fix a bug or typo. Refactor the code.
- Create third-party middleware - See instructions below.
- Share - Share your thoughts on the Blog, X, and others.
- Make your application - Please try to use Hono.

Note:
This project is started by Yusuke Wada ([@yusukebe](https://github.com/yusukebe)) for the hobby proposal.
It was just for fun. For now, this stance has not been changed basically.
I want to write the code as I like.
So, if you propose great ideas, but I do not appropriate them, the idea may not be accepted.

Although, don't worry!
Hono is tested well, polished by the contributors, and used by many developers. And I'll try my best to make Hono cool and hot, beautiful, and ultrafast.

## AI Usage Policy

You may use AI to contribute, but it must never waste a maintainer's time or make their work unpleasant.

To enforce this, and regardless of whether AI was actually used, a maintainer may close your PR without notice and block your account.

## Installing dependencies

The `honojs/hono` project uses [Bun](https://bun.sh/) as its package manager. Developers should install Bun.

After that, please install the dependency environment.

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

## PRs

Please ensure your PR passes tests with `bun run test`.

## Third-party middleware

Third-party middleware is not in the core.
It is allowed to depend on other libraries or work only in specific environments, such as Cloudflare Workers. For example:

- GraphQL Server middleware
- Firebase Auth middleware
- Sentry middleware

You can make a third-party middleware by yourself.
It may be under the "honojs organization" and distributed in the `@honojs` namespace.

The monorepo "[honojs/middleware](https://github.com/honojs/middleware)" manages these middleware.
If you want to do it, create an issue about your middleware.

## Local Development

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

task:
Adding an unrelated route can change duplicate path parameter values

### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.8. Also reproduced on current main (52febbcc).

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Node.js 25.2.1

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Both apps declare the same route and receive the same request. The second one only adds an unrelated `/a`.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { getRouterName } from 'hono/dev'

const a = new Hono()
a.get('/:id/:id/x', (c) => c.text(c.req.param('id')))
const resA = await a.request('/123/456/x')
console.log(await resA.text()) // 123
console.log(getRouterName(a))  // SmartRouter + RegExpRouter

const b = new Hono()
b.get('/:id/:id/x', (c) => c.text(c.req.param('id')))
b.get('/a', (c) => c.text('a'))
const resB = await b.request('/123/456/x')
console.log(await resB.text()) // 456
console.log(getRouterName(b))  // SmartRouter + TrieRouter
```

The request never reaches `/a`, but adding that route changes what `c.req.param('id')` returns.

### What is the expected behavior?

`c.req.param('id')` should not depend on which router `SmartRouter` picks.

In #1566 the first value was chosen when the same parameter name appears more than once in a path, and the shared router test still asserts it for `/:id/:id`:

```ts
it('self', () => {
  router.add('GET', '/:id/:id', 'foo')
  const res = match('GET', '/123/456')
  expect(res[0].params['id']).toBe('123')
})
```

### What do you see instead?

For `/:id/:id` and `/123/456`, `RegExpRouter`, `TrieRouter` and `LinearRouter` all return `123`. For `/:id/:id/x` and `/123/456/x`, `TrieRouter` returns `456` while the other two still return `123`.

With `/:id/:id/:id` and `/1/2/3` `TrieRouter` returns `2`, so it is not taking the last value either.

Under the default `SmartRouter`, adding `/a` switches the selection from `RegExpRouter` to `TrieRouter`, so the same request to the same route returns a different parameter value.

### Additional information

I traced this to `TrieRouter`. For `/:id/:id/x` the duplicate `id` gets overwritten while traversing the trie, and the two-segment case is handled differently in the final matching step.

That seems to be why `/:id/:id` returns `123` but `/:id/:id/x` returns `456`.

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `bun run format:fix && bun run lint:fix` to format the code

## Summary

Fixes #5422.

`TrieRouter` did not consistently keep the **first** value when the same path parameter name appeared more than once (e.g. `/:id/:id/x`). `RegExpRouter` / `LinearRouter` already follow first-wins, and `src/router/common.case.test.ts` asserts that for `/:id/:id`. For longer paths the trie overwrite left a different value, so `SmartRouter` could change `c.req.param('id')` merely by registering an unrelated route that switches the selected router.

### Root cause

In `src/router/trie-router/node.ts`, `search()` assigned `params[name] = part` (and the regexp-matcher equivalent), overwriting earlier values for the same name. That made `/:id/:id/x` return the second segment and `/:id/:id/:id` return the middle one.

### Fix

Record a path param only if that name is not already an own property (`Object.hasOwn`). Nullish assignment (`??=`) alone is not enough because a normal `{}` already has `constructor` on the prototype (caught by the reserved-words suite).

Tests extended in shared router cases, TrieRouter node tests, and a SmartRouter/`Hono` integration case that matches the issue reproduction.

# Contribution Guide

Contributions Welcome! We will be glad for your help.
You can contribute in the following ways.

- Create an Issue - Propose a new feature. Report a bug.
- Pull Request - Fix a bug or typo. Refactor the code.
- Create third-party middleware - See instructions below.
- Share - Share your thoughts on the Blog, X, and others.
- Make your application - Please try to use Hono.

Note:
This project is started by Yusuke Wada ([@yusukebe](https://github.com/yusukebe)) for the hobby proposal.
It was just for fun. For now, this stance has not been changed basically.
I want to write the code as I like.
So, if you propose great ideas, but I do not appropriate them, the idea may not be accepted.

Although, don't worry!
Hono is tested well, polished by the contributors, and used by many developers. And I'll try my best to make Hono cool and hot, beautiful, and ultrafast.

## AI Usage Policy

You may use AI to contribute, but it must never waste a maintainer's time or make their work unpleasant.

To enforce this, and regardless of whether AI was actually used, a maintainer may close your PR without notice and block your account.

## Installing dependencies

The `honojs/hono` project uses [Bun](https://bun.sh/) as its package manager. Developers should install Bun.

After that, please install the dependency environment.

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

## PRs

Please ensure your PR passes tests with `bun run test`.

## Third-party middleware

Third-party middleware is not in the core.
It is allowed to depend on other libraries or work only in specific environments, such as Cloudflare Workers. For example:

- GraphQL Server middleware
- Firebase Auth middleware
- Sentry middleware

You can make a third-party middleware by yourself.
It may be under the "honojs organization" and distributed in the `@honojs` namespace.

The monorepo "[honojs/middleware](https://github.com/honojs/middleware)" manages these middleware.
If you want to do it, create an issue about your middleware.

## Local Development

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

fix(router): handle slashes after regex quantifiers

Route patterns such as `/x/:prefix{a{2}/b}/x` should match `/x/aa/b/x`, capturing `aa/b` as `prefix`.

Currently, pattern masking stops at the quantifier’s closing `}`, leaving the following `/` exposed to path splitting.

This is a fairly rare edge case, so I hesitated over whether it was worth adding code to support it. However, the routing syntax allows this pattern, so I’m opening this PR.

task:
fix(helper/route): match regex params in basePath() the same way as the router

`basePath()` from `hono/route` drops a regex param when the next segment of the mount path is not static. `getPattern()` returns `^re$` for such a param, and `basePath()` matches that against the whole rest of the request path. The match fails, so the segment is skipped. The router still matches the request because it falls back to testing the current segment alone.

```ts
const sub = new Hono()
sub.get('/posts/:id', (c) => c.text(basePath(c)))
app.route('/api/:version{v[0-9]+}', sub)
// GET /api/v2/posts/123 -> '/api/' (expected '/api/v2')
```

If another param follows, the later segments shift too: `/users/:name{[a-z]+}/:group` returns `/users/abc` for `/users/abc/def/...`. `methodNotAllowed` relies on `basePath()`, so with `app.route('/:version{v[0-9]+}', api)` a `POST /v2/posts` returns 404 instead of 405.

This PR adds the router's single-segment fallback to `basePath()`. Plain params, wildcards and regex params followed by a static segment work as before.

- Ran: `pnpm exec vp test --run --project main src/helper/route src/middleware/method-not-allowed`. 29 passed. The new test fails on main with `'/api/'`.

Third-party middleware is not in the core.

```bash

fix(helper/route): match regex params in basePath() the same way as the router

`basePath()` from `hono/route` drops a regex param when the next segment of the mount path is not static. `getPattern()` returns `^re$` for such a param, and `basePath()` matches that against the whole rest of the request path. The match fails, so the segment is skipped. The router still matches the request because it falls back to testing the current segment alone.

sub.get('/posts/:id', (c) => c.text(basePath(c)))
app.route('/api/:version{v[0-9]+}', sub)
// GET /api/v2/posts/123 -> '/api/' (expected '/api/v2')
```

If another param follows, the later segments shift too: `/users/:name{[a-z]+}/:group` returns `/users/abc` for `/users/abc/def/...`. `methodNotAllowed` relies on `basePath()`, so with `app.route('/:version{v[0-9]+}', api)` a `POST /v2/posts` returns 404 instead of 405.

This PR adds the router's single-segment fallback to `basePath()`. Plain params, wildcards and regex params followed by a static segment work as before.

The match fails, so the segment is skipped. The router still matches the request because it falls back to testing the current segment alone.

```ts
const sub = new Hono()
sub.get('/posts/:id', (c) => c.text(basePath(c)))
app.route('/api/:version{v[0-9]+}', sub)
// GET /api/v2/posts/123 -> '/api/' (expected '/api/v2')
```

If another param follows, the later segments shift too: `/users/:name{[a-z]+}/:group` returns `/users/abc` for `/users/abc/def/...`. `methodNotAllowed` relies on `basePath()`, so with `app.route('/:version{v[0-9]+}', api)` a `POST /v2/posts` returns 404 instead of 405.

This PR adds the router's single-segment fallback to `basePath()`. Plain params, wildcards and regex params followed by a static segment work as before.

- Ran: `pnpm exec vp test --run --project main src/helper/route src/middleware/method-not-allowed`. 29 passed. The new test fails on main with `'/api/'`.

import { GET_MATCH_RESULT } from '../../request/constants'
import type { RouterRoute } from '../../types'
import { getPattern, splitRoutingPath } from '../../utils/url'

/**
 * Get matched routes in the handler
 *
 * @param {Context} c - The context object
 * @returns An array of matched routes
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * import { matchedRoutes } from 'hono/route'
 *
 * app.use('*', async function logger(c, next) {
 *   await next()
 *   matchedRoutes(c).forEach(({ handler, method, path }, i) => {
 *     const name = handler.name || (handler.length < 2 ? '[handler]' : '[middleware]')
 *     console.log(
 *       method,
 *       ' ',
 *       path,
 *       ' '.repeat(Math.max(10 - path.length, 0)),
 *       name,
 *       i === c.req.routeIndex ? '<- respond from here' : ''
 *     )
 *   })
 * })
 * ```
 */
export const matchedRoutes = (c: Context): RouterRoute[] =>
  // @ts-expect-error c.req[GET_MATCH_RESULT] is not typed
  (c.req as unknown)[GET_MATCH_RESULT][0].map(([[, route]]) => route)

/**
 * Get the route path registered within the handler
 *
 * @param {Context} c - The context object
 * @param {number} index - The index of the route from which to retrieve the path, similar to Array.prototype.at(), where a negative number is the index counted from the end of the matching route. Defaults to the current route index.
 * @returns The route path registered within the handler
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * import { routePath } from 'hono/route'
 *
 * app.use('*', (c, next) => {
 *   console.log(routePath(c)) // '*'
 *   console.log(routePath(c, -1)) // '/posts/:id'
 *   return next()
 * })
 *
 * app.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {
 *   return c.text(routePath(c)) // '/posts/:id'
 * })
 * ```
 */
export const routePath = (c: Context, index?: number): string =>
  matchedRoutes(c).at(index ?? c.req.routeIndex)?.path ?? ''

 *

 * import { baseRoutePath } from 'hono/route'
 *
 * const app = new Hono()
 *
 * const subApp = new Hono()
 * subApp.get('/posts/:id', (c) => {

 * })

 * app.route('/:sub', subApp)
 * ```
 */
export const baseRoutePath = (c: Context, index?: number): string =>
  matchedRoutes(c).at(index ?? c.req.routeIndex)?.basePath ?? ''

 * Get the basePath with embedded parameters
 *
 * @param {Context} c - The context object
 * @param {number} index - The index of the route from which to retrieve the path, similar to Array.prototype.at(), where a negative number is the index counted from the end of the matching route. Defaults to the current route index.

# Contribution Guide

Contributions Welcome! We will be glad for your help.
You can contribute in the following ways.

- Create an Issue - Propose a new feature. Report a bug.
- Pull Request - Fix a bug or typo. Refactor the code.
- Create third-party middleware - See instructions below.
- Share - Share your thoughts on the Blog, X, and others.
- Make your application - Please try to use Hono.

Note:
This project is started by Yusuke Wada ([@yusukebe](https://github.com/yusukebe)) for the hobby proposal.
It was just for fun. For now, this stance has not been changed basically.
I want to write the code as I like.
So, if you propose great ideas, but I do not appropriate them, the idea may not be accepted.

Although, don't worry!
Hono is tested well, polished by the contributors, and used by many developers. And I'll try my best to make Hono cool and hot, beautiful, and ultrafast.

## AI Usage Policy

You may use AI to contribute, but it must never waste a maintainer's time or make their work unpleasant.

To enforce this, and regardless of whether AI was actually used, a maintainer may close your PR without notice and block your account.

## Installing dependencies

The `honojs/hono` project uses [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) as its package manager, and [Bun](https://bun.sh/) to run the build and some of the tests. Developers should install both.

After that, please install the dependency environment.

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

## PRs

Please ensure your PR passes tests with `pnpm run test`.

## Third-party middleware

Third-party middleware is not in the core.
It is allowed to depend on other libraries or work only in specific environments, such as Cloudflare Workers. For example:

- GraphQL Server middleware
- Firebase Auth middleware
- Sentry middleware

You can make a third-party middleware by yourself.
It may be under the "honojs organization" and distributed in the `@honojs` namespace.

The monorepo "[honojs/middleware](https://github.com/honojs/middleware)" manages these middleware.
If you want to do it, create an issue about your middleware.

## Local Development

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

The `honojs/hono` project uses [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) as its package manager, and [Bun](https://bun.sh/) to run the build and some of the tests. Developers should install both.

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

Third-party middleware is not in the core.
It is allowed to depend on other libraries or work only in specific environments, such as Cloudflare Workers. For example:

- GraphQL Server middleware
- Firebase Auth middleware
- Sentry middleware

You can make a third-party middleware by yourself.
It may be under the "honojs organization" and distributed in the `@honojs` namespace.

If you want to do it, create an issue about your middleware.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:honojs/hono.git && cd hono && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```
